A Day in the Life: As a Front-End Team Member, your day is centered around creating a smooth and positive checkout experience for customers. You’re often the final stop before customers head home, helping complete their purchase accurately while keeping interactions friendly and efficient. Whether scanning items, bagging groceries, or answering questions, your role helps ensure each visit ends on a strong note. Another part of the role is keeping the front end organized, clean, and running consistently throughout the day. You’ll rotate between tasks like handling transactions, collecting carts, restocking supplies, and maintaining the checkout area. With a steady flow of customers and changing priorities, the work stays active, making it a good fit for someone who enjoys variety and staying engaged in a fast‑paced environment. What you bring to the table: Customer Interaction Skills: Friendly, clear communication during checkout and customer assistance Transaction Handling: Processing purchases accurately, including cash, card, and digital payments Attention to Detail: Accuracy in scanning, pricing, produce codes, and order completion Basic Math Skills: Handling cash transactions, counting change, and balancing registers Organization & Time Management: Managing multiple tasks while maintaining steady workflow Store Support Awareness: Assisting with bagging, cart retrieval, stocking, and general front‑end upkeep Problem Awareness: Recognizing and addressing pricing, transaction, or customer service questions Operational Awareness: Following company policies, register procedures, and checkout processes Adaptability: Comfort managing changing tasks and customer flow throughout the shift Physical Capability: Comfort with standing for extended periods, lifting up to 50 lbs., and working indoors and outdoors as needed Requirements: Must be 16 years of age or older (or 18 years of age or older, depending on local/state requirements) Completion of company cashier or front-end training upon hire Basic math and communication skills required Ability to work a flexible schedule including early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays Prior customer service experience preferred but not required Why you will choose us: Albertsons Companies Inc. has always been a people-oriented business, and thoughtful people practices remain a core element of our company’s philosophy. Our goal is to continue to bring people together around the joys of food and to inspire well-being and that starts with people like you bringing your unique self to our company and making it one person stronger and better! We also provide a variety of benefits including: Inclusive work culture built on belonging Competitive Wages paid weekly Flexible work schedules Associate discounts Leaders invested in your training, career growth & development. Health and welfare benefits for eligible employees (Medical, Dental, 401k and more!) Vacation / Paid Time Off Our Values We put people first. We are customer driven. We value different perspectives. We raise the bar. We act as owners. We are one team. We build belonging. We are committed to a healthy future.

### About the Role Join the perception engineering team at an early-stage industrial automation startup, building computer vision systems for manufacturing quality inspection. You will work on real factory applications that identify parts and process steps, helping catch assembly errors before they lead to rework or defects. ### What You'll Do - Build and improve computer vision pipelines for detection, classification, tracking, and temporal understanding. - Test first-person perception in challenging conditions such as camera motion, occlusion, motion blur, and changing lighting. - Use synthetic and real-world data to find failure cases and improve model performance. - Train, evaluate, and debug vision models in PyTorch. - Explore geometric vision, calibration, localization, pose estimation, and 3D perception. - Optimize models for low-latency inference and edge deployment, and build tools to evaluate real-world performance. - Support factory deployments and learn from system performance on the shop floor. ### What We're Looking For - You are studying computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field, and are interested in computer vision and physical AI. - You are comfortable with Python and have hands-on experience in computer vision, machine learning, or robotics. - Experience with PyTorch, OpenCV, object detection, tracking, synthetic data, SLAM or VIO, 3D vision, CUDA or TensorRT, ROS2, or NVIDIA Jetson is helpful. - You have built and debugged technical projects and are ready to learn quickly and take ownership. ### Compensation & Benefits Visa sponsorship is available. Relocation from Germany is supported. ### Location On-site in San Francisco, California, United States.

# **Building Healthcare That Remembers** Every time you call a doctor's office, the system forgets you the moment you hang up. You wait on hold, explain everything from scratch, get bounced between lines, and hope someone follows up. Everyone has felt this. No one should have to. At Assort Health, we're building one continuous conversation for every patient. An AI agent that knows who you are, remembers how you like to be reached, and carries that context from your first symptom to your full recovery. What began as the first voice AI agent to schedule a specialty appointment has become the largest proprietary specialty dataset in healthcare: 285 million patient interactions, 62,000 care protocols, 1.6 million decision pathways. We went from 15 people in 2025 and will cross 250 by the end of 2026. Revenue is up 20x in 15 months and we've raised $222 million, including a recent [$120 million Series C](https://www.assorthealth.com/blog/assort-health-raises-120-million-series-c-to-scale-largest-deployment-of-ai-agents-for-the-patient-journey) at a $1.2 billion valuation. We've also been named to the Forbes Cloud 100 and the 2026 Enterprise Tech 30 as the only healthcare AI company on the list! Healthcare spends $1.1 trillion a year on administration instead of care. If you want to help change that, apply below. ## About the Role We're on the hunt for driven and scrappy product-minded engineering interns to join our team at an exciting stage of our startup's journey. If you're eager to build products, tackle challenging problems, and see your work reach real users, this is an opportunity to make a significant impact. You'll gain hands-on experience in a dynamic startup environment, working with cutting-edge generative AI and voice/transcription models and technologies. As part of our engineering team, you'll work alongside experienced engineers to take ideas from zero to one. You'll own meaningful projects, contribute to product decisions, and learn what it takes to build and scale software for healthcare professionals. If you're a self-starter who likes to experiment, figure things out, and ship, you'll fit right in. You'll have plenty of autonomy, with guidance and feedback from the team as you navigate new challenges. **The anticipated dates for this role are January 11th - April 30th.** ## What You'll Do - Work closely with our engineering team to build features and products from the ground up. - Own a scoped project from initial design through implementation, testing, and deployment, with support from experienced engineers. - Explore and apply generative AI and voice/transcription technologies to solve real problems for healthcare professionals. - Participate actively in product, design, and development discussions, contributing fresh ideas and perspectives. - Learn from healthcare professionals and translate their feedback into thoughtful product improvements. - Help develop secure, scalable software that meets our HIPAA compliance and security requirements. ## What We're Looking For - Pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in computer science or a related field - Strong engineering fundamentals and experience building software through coursework, personal projects, open-source contributions, or previous internships. - Strong technical problem-solving skills and comfort working through ambiguity in a fast-moving startup environment. - Willingness to wear multiple hats, from understanding user needs and designing features to writing code, testing, and debugging. - Curiosity, openness to feedback, and a willingness to learn through rapid iteration and experimentation. - Bonus points for experience with React, TypeScript, or Go; building or deploying AI/LLM applications; or working with evaluation frameworks, agent tooling, RAG pipelines, and prompt engineering. # **Benefits & Perks for Assorties** - **💸 Competitive Compensation** – Including salary *and* employee stock options so you share in our success. - **📚 Lifelong Learning** – Annual budget for professional development, plus training opportunities to help you grow. - **💻 Office Setup Stipend** – We’ll outfit your in-office workspace so comfy as it's productive. - **🩺 Top-Tier Health Coverage** – Medical, dental, and vision insurance, because your health comes first. - **🏖 Flexible PTO** – We trust you to take the time you need to recharge and come back ready to crush it. - **🥗 Meals & Snacks** – Lunch, dinner, and snack breaks that fuel great ideas. - **💪 Fitness Stipend** – Your wellness matters. We reimburse monthly membership costs to support your health. - 🚆 **Commuter Benefits** – We cover eligible transportation costs to make your trip to work easier. - **👵 401(k)** – Build your retirement savings. # How We Work & What We Value Our team at Assort Health moves fast, stays focused, and is fueled by a desire to serve our customers and patients. Our company values guide *how* we work—they are present in how we show up, make decisions and work together to move our mission forward. We bring a **Day One Drive**, relentlessly striving to improve, keep a **5-Star Focus**, as our customers are our lifeblood, always **Answer the Call**, remembering that ownership and accountability are paramount, and show up with **One Pulse**, because we are one team, with one rhythm and one result. Our team is growing and we are looking for motivated, hardworking, and passionate talent. If you want to make healthcare accessible for everyone, we’d love to hear from you! **Please note:** the Assort Health Talent Team will only email you from an [](http://assorthealth.com) email address.

role: Adjunct Lecturer, Technology Integration in Project Management  (On-Campus, Spring 2027 & Future Semesters)

Students will gain hands-on experience with project management information systems (PMIS) and enterprise platforms such as MS Project, Asana, Trello, SAP, and Oracle Primavera, while also learning to leverage AI, automation, and data analytics tools like Power BI to enhance decision-making and performance monitoring. The course emphasizes the use of agile and hybrid methodologies supported by tech-enabled tools, preparing students to lead projects with efficiency, adaptability, and innovation in digitally driven organizations. Responsibilities Lead in-person class lectures, instructional activities, and classroom discussions Evaluate student work and grade assignments Monitor student concerns and inquiries, and be the first point of contact for student questions Hold weekly office hours Prepare, maintain, and enhance the course in Canvas, Columbia University’s learning management system for onsite and online courses Part‐time Lecturers who are new to SPS must complete Canvas training (online learning management system) Attend Project Management faculty meetings If assigned to design the course, responsibilities also include: Develop course objectives that align with program-wide learning outcomes Create activity maps tying course activities to objectives, ensuring industry relevance Draft a detailed syllabus (course description, schedule, grading rubric, and assessments) for review and approval by the Program Curriculum Committee and the Committee on Instruction (COI). Collaborate with Instructional Design to develop course materials through a consultative process. This includes partnering on course development (aligning objectives, materials, and assessments), creating dynamic instructional media (videos, infographics, and interactive resources), maintaining established courses with updates and troubleshooting, and receiving just-in-time assistance for targeted needs. Serving as an adjunct Lecturer provides an outstanding opportunity to educate and mentor students in the field of project management as well as to form a rewarding professional relationship with Columbia University’s world-class faculty. Columbia University SPS operates under a scholar-practitioner faculty model, which enables students to learn from faculty that have outstanding academic training as well as a record of accomplishment as practitioners in an applied professional setting. Requirements A master’s degree in engineering (e.g., civil, mechanical, or industrial), construction management, project management, operations research, technology management, business analytics, or data science (with a project management focus) At least 8 years of experience in roles such as IT Project Manager, Technology Consultant, Digital Transformation Lead, or Systems Engineer Hands-on experience with software selection, implementation, and integration in a project setting Experience in cross-functional technology deployment across sectors (e.g., construction, manufacturing, tech, services) PMP or equivalent certifications preferred A passion for teaching, strong interpersonal and communication skills, and the ability to connect academic material to contemporary industry practices. Preferred Skills & Experience A terminal degree in one of the above mentioned disciplines 2+ years graduate-level university teaching experience Compensation Range - $10,000 - $15,000 per semester-length course. Review of applications begins immediately and will continue until positions are filled. All applicants, please provide: A resume/CV inclusive of university teaching experience -- highlight teaching at the graduate level A cover letter Evidence of teaching effectiveness (e.g., student evaluations of teaching, teaching observation summaries, etc.) All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Columbia University is an Equal Opportunity Employer / Disability / Veteran Columbia University has been a leader in higher education in the nation and around the world for more than 250 years. ### **About the Role** The Speculative Decoding team at Together AI builds the draft models and algorithms that let large language models generate faster without changing their outputs. Our speculators run in production on frontier open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Our work sits at the intersection of model training, inference algorithms and serving systems, and we co-design all three to lower the cost and latency of generation. As a research intern, you will dive into open questions in speculative decoding: new drafter architectures and verification schemes, knowledge distillation and training recipes that align draft and target models, and drafters that adapt as traffic shifts. You will train and fine-tune draft models at scale on dedicated GPU clusters, and test your ideas against realistic serving workloads, including long-context and agentic traffic. Projects aim to answer important research questions in speculative decoding, enabling faster generation on frontier models, drafters that keep pace with changing workloads, and robust, reproducible evaluation under real traffic. ### Past Research Speculative decoding research by Together researchers, interns and academic collaborators includes: - [Speculative Speculative Decoding](https://openreview.net/forum?id=aL1Wnml9Ef) (ICLR 2026) - [When RL Meets Adaptive Speculative Training: A Unified Training-Serving System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06932) (ICML 2026) - [Beat the Long Tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13841) (MLSys 2026) ### **Responsibilities** - Research and prototype new efficient speculative decoding algorithms and draft model architectures - Train, fine-tune and distill draft models, and design rigorous experiments to validate hypotheses. - Implement optimized version for serving engines to show efficacy in real world workloads - Communicate the plans, progress, and results of projects to the broader team - Share findings through technical write-ups and blog posts, and help bring successful ideas into production ### **Requirements** - Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field - Strong knowledge of Machine Learning and Deep Learning fundamentals - Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning large models with distributed training frameworks (e.g., Megatron-LM, FSDP) - Familiarity with modern model architectures, such as Mixture-of-Experts and hybrid attention ### Preferred Qualifications - Prior research experience in speculative decoding, efficient inference, or efficient machine learning - Publications at leading conferences in machine learning or systems (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys) - Experience with knowledge distillation, post-training, or reinforcement learning - Familiarity with LLM serving engines (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) - Contributions to open-source machine learning projects ### **About Together AI** Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month. ### **Internship Program Details** Our internship program runs 12 to 14 weeks, giving you the opportunity to work alongside industry-leading engineers and researchers across multiple teams. This cohort's internship dates span January 4th to April 9th. ### **Compensation** We offer competitive compensation, housing stipends, and other competitive benefits. The estimated US hourly rate for this role is $58 - $70 an hour. Our hourly rates are determined by location, level and role. Individual compensation will be determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. ### **Equal Opportunity** Together AI is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is proud to offer equal employment opportunity to everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, and more. **PhD Internship 2027: Research - Boston Research - Boston** Boston, US | Full-time | Fixed-term| Hybrid Salary: $55.70 per hour, DOE **About us** Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in materials and climate science to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved. Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent, and passion. Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast. **About the role** Delivering practical quantum error correction requires tightly integrated quantum and classical systems. The quantum hardware connectivity, its physical error rates, circuit compilation and compatible QEC codes all affect performance. On the classical side, decoding algorithms must process large volumes of error data within demanding latency, bandwidth, compute, and power constraints. As a Research Intern, you will investigate simulating, running and decoding QEC experiments. Along with your supervisor, you will frame a research project. Your project will sit at the intersection of quantum error correction, computer simulations, computer architecture and hardware-software co-design. Depending on the project, you could study noise models for quantum hardware, work on efficient simulations for QEC experiments, explore efficient QEC decoding or predecoding methods, model the classical resources required by fault-tolerant quantum programs, or investigate how decoding workloads can be distributed across different levels of a computing system. You will work alongside Riverlane’s quantum scientists and engineers in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with support from a dedicated supervisor. Your work will contribute to our understanding of how QEC systems can meet the performance requirements of increasingly large quantum computers. **What you will do** - Develop algorithms, simulations or architectural models to evaluate potential approaches - Investigate methods for reducing the compute, communication, memory, latency or power requirements associated with QEC - Explore trade-offs between decoding performance, logical error suppression and classical resource requirements - Collaborate with quantum scientists and engineers working across QEC theory, decoding, software and hardware - Analyse results and communicate your findings through technical discussions, presentations and written reports - Produce clear, reproducible research code and supporting documentation **What we need** - You must be currently pursuing a PhD in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or another related technical field - Research experience in at least one of the following areas: - Running quantum circuits on quantum hardware - Decoding algorithms or quantum error-correcting codes - Experience developing computational models, simulations or research software - Proficiency in Python, C, C++ or another relevant programming language - A strong understanding of computer systems and architecture - Computer architecture or quantum-classical systems - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills - The ability to communicate complex technical ideas clearly - The ability to take initiative and work effectively with researchers and engineers from different disciplines - Authorization to work in the United States for the duration of the internship **Even better if…** - You have experience researching qLDPC or surface codes - You are familiar with QEC decoding or predecoding techniques - You have explored the classical resource requirements of fault-tolerant quantum computing - You have experience with scientific computing, quantum circuit simulation or QEC simulation tools - You have contributed to academic publications, open-source software or collaborative research projects - You have experience with hardware-software or compiler-hardware co-design - You understand the latency, bandwidth or power constraints affecting quantum control and decoding systems **Important notes** - description: **Build your civil engineering career in site design.** You'll work on real land development projects, design real sites, and grow through hands-on experience, professional development, and mentorship from engineers who want to see you succeed. **About the Role** Bohler’s West Palm Beach, FL office is seeking an Entry Level Civil Engineer (Land Development) who is eager to learn, grow, and make a positive impact. In this role, you will work closely with engineers, designers, and project managers to bring exciting land development projects to life, including site planning, grading, utilities, and stormwater management. You will contribute to projects for well-known brands across commercial, residential, and mixed-use markets, all while laying the groundwork for a rewarding engineering career. **What You’ll Do** - Work on a variety of land development projects, including commercial, residential, industrial, and mixed-use sites - Partner with experienced engineers and mentors to learn every stage of site design, from concept through construction - Use AutoCAD Civil 3D to create site layouts, grading plans, and utility designs - Research and interpret design manuals, zoning ordinances, and jurisdictional regulations - Review and address regulatory comments and assist with project redesigns as needed - Support the preparation of stormwater management reports and construction submittals - Participate in professional and technical training through Bohler’s Learning & Development programs - Attend site visits to observe field conditions and coordinate with project teams - Engage in civic, professional, and business organizations to build your network - Perform other responsibilities in accordance with company policies and standards **What We Offer** - A supportive and flexible work environment that empowers employees to stay healthy, fulfill their passions, and balance work and life goals - The opportunity to take ownership of your career with an unsurpassed focus on career development and mentorship - A Learning & Development department that facilitates ongoing technical and professional growth, including individualized AutoCAD Civil 3D training - Complete visibility and exposure to all aspects of land development projects - The chance to immerse yourself in the design process while working side-by-side with talented teammates - Open and transparent communication with senior leadership and local office management - Team-building activities, office events, and a collaborative, high-energy environment **What You’ll Bring** - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field - 0–1+ years of residential, commercial, or industrial site design and permitting experience - Familiarity with AutoCAD Civil 3D (preferred; training provided if not yet proficient) - Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to teamwork - Motivation to take initiative and contribute to shared goals - EIT certification is helpful but not required **Get hands-on experience contributing to real projects, and see how your work helps shape communities and your career.** #LI-Onsite

Our partner is looking for a Machine Learning Engineer, New Grad – Quora based in the United States.** Launch your machine learning career by helping build AI-powered systems that improve content quality and safety across a global knowledge-sharing platform. In this role, you will collaborate with experienced engineers to design, develop, evaluate, and deploy large language model (LLM)-powered agents that identify harmful content, detect abuse, and automate complex moderation tasks. You will work on challenging machine learning problems at scale, with opportunities to experiment with emerging AI technologies and contribute to systems serving millions of users. As part of a small, collaborative engineering team, you will take ownership of meaningful projects and follow them from early development through production deployment. You will evaluate model performance, investigate failure cases, and continuously improve the accuracy, reliability, and efficiency of AI-driven solutions. This remote opportunity is ideal for a recent graduate or emerging engineer with a strong technical foundation, a curiosity for AI innovation, and a passion for building safer online experiences. ### Accountabilities - Design, build, and deploy LLM-powered agents that detect and address spam, harassment, and other policy-violating content across a large-scale online platform. - Develop agentic workflows that automate complex content moderation and user safety tasks, improving the efficiency, consistency, and effectiveness of existing systems. - Build and enhance machine learning models and AI-powered systems that adapt to evolving abuse patterns, emerging threats, and changing content safety challenges. - Evaluate model and agent performance through offline testing, online experiments, and production monitoring, balancing accuracy, reliability, latency, and computational costs. - Investigate model failures, analyze edge cases, conduct experiments, and refine technical approaches to improve system quality and overall performance. - Identify new opportunities to apply machine learning, large language models, and emerging AI techniques to content quality, platform integrity, and user safety. - Collaborate closely with experienced machine learning engineers and cross-functional colleagues to develop practical solutions to complex technical challenges. - Take ownership of projects throughout the engineering lifecycle, from problem identification and experimentation to implementation, deployment, and ongoing optimization. - Contribute to a culture of continuous learning, technical experimentation, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving. - Help develop scalable, reliable, and cost-effective AI systems that support a positive user experience and protect the integrity of a global knowledge-sharing community. ## Requirements - A bachelor's, master's, or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, either completed or currently in progress. - Strong understanding of the mathematical foundations underlying machine learning algorithms and their practical applications. - Coursework, research, or project experience involving large language model applications, transformer architectures, or related AI technologies. - Strong programming skills in Python and the ability to develop, test, and maintain reliable code. - Genuine enthusiasm for learning, experimenting with new technologies, and continuously improving both individual and team performance. - Availability to begin full-time employment in early 2027. - Ability to participate in meetings and spontaneous collaboration during the team's coordination hours, Monday through Friday, from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Pacific Time. - Previous software engineering experience through an internship, professional role, open-source contribution, or coding competition is preferred. - Practical experience building, implementing, or evaluating LLM-powered agents through academic projects, research, internships, or production systems is an advantage. - Familiarity with AI-assisted coding tools, such as Claude Code or Codex, preferably through regular hands-on use. - Coursework, research, or project experience in natural language processing (NLP) is beneficial. - Familiarity with machine learning frameworks and infrastructure, including PyTorch, TensorFlow, Spark, or Kubernetes, is an advantage. - A genuine interest in content safety, online community quality, and the responsible application of artificial intelligence. - Strong analytical thinking, curiosity, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate technical issues and develop evidence-based solutions. - A collaborative mindset and willingness to learn from experienced colleagues, share ideas, and contribute to a high-performing engineering team. - An interest in supporting a mission centered on expanding access to knowledge and creating positive online experiences. - Candidates from diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply, including those who may not meet every preferred qualification but demonstrate strong technical potential and a passion for machine learning. ## Benefits - **Paid time off:** Time away from work to support rest, personal commitments, and work-life balance. - **Employee assistance programs:** Resources designed to support employee well-being. - **Professional development:** Opportunities to learn from experienced machine learning engineers and contribute to challenging, real-world AI projects. - **Hands-on AI innovation:** Exposure to large language models, agentic workflows, production machine learning systems, and modern engineering tools. - **Meaningful technical impact:** The opportunity to develop AI systems that improve content quality, detect harmful behavior, and help create safer online communities. - **Inclusive culture:** A collaborative environment that values diverse perspectives, experimentation, transparency, and continuous learning.

role: Research Intern (Academic Credit) - Department of Neurology - Per Diem (On-site)
description: About Us: We are a leading research institution committed to advancing scientific knowledge and innovation. Our team is dedicated to conducting ground breaking research and providing meaningful learning opportunities for aspiring scientists. Join us and contribute to our mission while gaining invaluable experience in a dynamic and collaborative environment. The Research Internship program provides students and trainees an opportunity to develop basic research skills. Interns in this program are provided the opportunity to experience and observe many different aspects of basic, translational and/or clinical research. This program offers interns a unique experience, which is intended to provide a wealth of knowledge about the numerous options for a career in healthcare research. Typically lasting not more than a twelve-month period, this internship will expose participants to a diverse spectrum of clinical and non-clinical based research investigations. Under direct supervision from the assigned Postdoctoral Scientist, senior-level Research Associate and/or Principal Investigator, the intern will be provided with basic research instruction, will be oriented to the Institutional Review Board and other Human Subjects courses, and will be introduced to new and innovative research practices and techniques. Overview of Department & Mentor The Goldrich Center for Alzheimer’s and Memory Disorders clinic occupies 15,000 square feet on the 6th floor of the Cedars-Sinai the Advanced Health Sciences Pavilion (AHSP) building, which contains 100,000 square feet of state-of-the-art wet lab and supporting space for neuroscience and neurology related research. The Center oversees the care of over 500 patients per year, has two fellowship-trained behavioral neurology and neuropsychiatry specialists, one fellowship trained geriatric medicine specialist, one fellowship trained geriatric psychiatrist, three memory disorders nurse practitioners, one behavioral neurology and neuropsychiatry fellow, two neuropsychologists specializing in memory disorders, and one dedicated social worker. Center research personnel include one research manager and one memory disorders clinical research coordinator. Dr. Mitzi Gonzales is an Associate Professor of the Department of Neurology and the Director of Translational Research for the Goldrich Center for Alzheimer’s and Memory Disorders at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. She is a board-certified clinical neuropsychologist and clinician scientist, who has led and collaborated on large-scale research efforts evaluating plasma proteins, sensory-motor functioning, and broader aging phenotypes as biomarkers for neurodegenerative disease risk. Dr. Sarah Kremen is an Associate Professor of the Department of Neurology, where she serves as the Director of the Neurobehavior Program in the Department of Neurology and the Goldrich Alzheimer’s and Memory Disorders Center. She is a board-certified neurologist with subspecialty training in Neurobehavior and Neuropsychiatry. Dr. Kremen’s research focuses on clinicopathological correlation in neurodegenerative diseases, Alzheimer’s disease clinical trials, and the lived impact of implementation of new diagnostics and therapies. Dr. Gonzales and Dr. Kremen co-lead for the Goldrich Observational ADRD Longitudinal studies, which the visiting scholar will partake in. Role Activities & Timeline January 15th - January 31st: Human subjects training; research ethics, fundamentals of the informed consent process February 1st – February 14th: Clinical research study design review; discussion of observational research projects; protocol review February 15th – March 14th: Overview community-engaged research, introduction to neurodegenerative diseases; observations of observational clinical research procedures; attendance at outreach events; attend consensus reviews and team meetings; introduction to data coding, REDCap; research literature review March 15th – April 14th: Introduction to cognitive assessments; hands on administration practice; observations of observational clinical research procedures; attendance at outreach events; attend consensus reviews and team meetings; data quality assurance and management; research hypothesis generation April 15th – May 15th: Observations of observational clinical research procedures; attendance at outreach events; attend consensus reviews and team meetings; research hypothesis testing and basic statistics, research abstract writing All weeks: mentorship in clinical trial design, implementation, data management, statistics, and abstract writing Systems Access: N/A Role Summary & Objectives The Research Intern will have the opportunity to work with an interdisciplinary team of neuropsychologists, neurologists, geriatricians, and clinical researchers with expertise in aging and Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD). The Research Intern will be immersed in the clinical research process, gaining experience on study design and implementation. The Research Intern will be able to partake in two clinical research studies. The first, the GOAL Study, is an internally funded project that aims to establish a longitudinal cohort of individuals of across the ADRD continuum. The second is the RAPID study, which deploys brief cognitive testing and questionnaires relevant to ADRD. The Research Intern will learn fundamental skills relevant to clinical research in aging and ADRD including best practices for the informed consent process, human subjects' protection, clinical cohort study design, and community-based participatory research engagement. The overarching goal is to provide foundational clinical research skills that the successful candidate can utilize to develop independent research projects in the future. In addition, the Research Intern will learn data management skills using REDCap, basic statistical analyses, hypothesis development, and abstract writing. The successful candidate will develop and implement a clinical research project that can be completed utilizing existing datasets and will produce an abstract that can be submitted to a local or national research conference. Required Education & Experience Must be 18 years of age or older. Must have a HS Diploma or GED. Must reside in the greater Los Angeles area or surrounding cities while conducting all activities related to the intern or visitor appointment. INTERNS: Those participating for academic credit must receive academic credit for the duration of the internship.

role: Research Intern - Efficient AI Software Systems
description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. Researchers in artificial intelligence (AI) are building systems that can reason, plan and act on behalf of the people who use them, from writing software to automating complex, multistep tasks. As these systems become more capable and more widely used, making them efficient matters more and more. That means getting the most value from the compute they use, choosing the right capabilities for each task, and adapting to the needs of the people and environments they serve. Microsoft's deep investments in the field are advancing the state of the art in efficient and agentic AI. Its researchers combine machine learning, systems research and rigorous empirical evaluation to understand how intelligent systems can balance quality, speed and cost, and how they can improve with experience. The research, tools and services that result are woven into existing and new products and, at the same time, made open and accessible to the broader community in a bid to accelerate innovation, democratize AI and help developers and organizations do more with the resources they have. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** #### Required Qualifications - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, STEM, or a relevant field. #### **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. #### #### Preferred Qualifications - 1+ year(s) of experience (classroom or work-related) in one or more of the following areas: machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, large language models, AI agents, or machine learning systems. - 1+ completed courses in probability and statistics, machine learning, or optimization. - Experience conducting research on the efficiency, cost, or performance of machine learning models or systems (e.g., inference optimization, model selection, model compression, or adaptive computation). - Experience building or evaluating applications or agents that use large language models. - Experience designing benchmarks or experiments to evaluate machine learning systems, and analyzing quantitative results. - Experience comparing alternative methods, prototypes, or analytical approaches to address a research or applied problem. - Experience collaborating with researchers or engineering teams on a research or applied project. - Prior research experience evidenced by publications, preprints, or open-source research projects. - Experience communicating research findings through a presentation, poster, report, or publication. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. --- Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. ## **About Abridge** Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients. Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems. We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh. ## **The Role** We're looking for Software Engineering Interns to join Abridge's Engineering team for a 3-month internship program in Fall 2026, Spring 2027, or Summer 2027 with the possibility of extension. You'll collaborate with our engineering team to build and ship real-world features that translate cutting-edge language model capabilities into dependable clinical systems. With mentorship and guidance, you'll gain hands-on experience designing, coding, and releasing AI-powered software that makes a meaningful impact on clinicians' workflows. **What You'll Do** - Design and build end-to-end features, enhancing our existing systems and contributing to agentic LLM workflows (retrieval pipelines, structured tool use, chained LLM calls) - Fix user-facing bugs and issues, and make quality-of-life improvements across our backend and frontend systems - Get hands-on with evaluation frameworks that measure accuracy, robustness, and clinical reliability - Help prototype with new models, prompting techniques, and open-source orchestration tools (LangChain, LlamaIndex, etc.) - Develop a strong user-centric mindset, building empathy for Abridge's clinicians and the challenges they face - Collaborate across cross-functional product teams — design, product, machine learning, and infrastructure — to ship features to our customers - Receive guidance from an experienced software engineering mentor, and collaborate one-on-one with teammates within your pod **What You'll Bring** - A strong interest in pursuing a full-time software engineering role in 2027 or 2028 — high-performing interns are eligible to receive a return offer - AI tooling is already part of how you work — you use it to write, debug, and learn faster, and you know when to trust it vs. verify - Passion for and understanding of Abridge's mission - A curious, adaptable, and proactive mindset, with a desire to learn and grow in a fast-paced startup environment - A collaborative, low-ego mindset — we move fast, and we need team players who are eager to contribute wherever needed **Base Salary:** $40/hr Must be willing to work from our San Francisco (Potrero) office 5x per week. This internship is based in our San Francisco office. Relocation to SF will be supported through reimbursements. ## **Why Work at Abridge?** At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month. Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business. Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients. We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life. If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you. ## **How we take care of Abridgers:** - **Generous Time Off**: 14 paid holidays, flexible PTO for salaried employees, and accrued time off for hourly employees - **Comprehensive Health Plans**: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for all full-time employees and their families. - **Generous HSA Contribution**: If you choose a High Deductible Health Plan, Abridge makes monthly contributions to your HSA. - **Paid Parental Leave**: Generous paid parental leave for all full-time employees. - **Family Forming Benefits:** Resources and financial support to help you build your family. - **401(k) Matching**: Contribution matching to help invest in your future. - **Personal Device Allowance**: Tax free funds for personal device usage. - **Pre-tax Benefits:** Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Commuter Benefits. - **Lifestyle Wallet**: Monthly contributions for fitness, professional development, coworking, and more. - **Mental Health Support**: Dedicated access to therapy and coaching to help you reach your goals. - **Sabbatical Leave**: Paid Sabbatical Leave after 5 years of employment. - **Compensation and Equity**: Competitive compensation and equity grants for full time employees. - ... and much more! ## **Equal Opportunity Employer** Abridge is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants equally without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability. We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the interview process. Once you submit your application, we'll follow up with details on how to request an accommodation for interviewing, completing any assessments, or otherwise participating in the selection process. ## **Staying safe - Protect yourself from recruitment fraud** We are aware of individuals and entities fraudulently representing themselves as Abridge recruiters and/or hiring managers. Abridge will never ask for financial information or payment, or for personal information such as bank account number or social security number during the job application or interview process. Any emails from the Abridge recruiting team will come from an @[](http://abridge.com) email address. You can learn more about how to protect yourself from these types of fraud by referring to [this article](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/05/scammers-are-hijacking-job-ads-heres-how-spot-fakes). Please exercise caution and cease communications if something feels suspicious about your interactions.

## **About Cowboy Space** **Mission:** Cowboy Space Corporation is solving the global energy crisis by building the infrastructure for abundant, resilient space-based solar energy. We are tackling one of humanity’s most complex engineering challenges with a world-class team dedicated to delivering a revolutionary power platform. Cowboy Space Corporation is transforming how civilization powers, computes and connects - from orbit to Earth. **Background**: Cowboy Space Corporation is building the infrastructure to power and connect the orbital economy. Our modular, scalable satellites collect sunlight in Low Earth Orbit to enable multiple integrated applications: transmitting energy via infrared lasers (space-to-earth and space-to-space), powering on-orbit high-performance computing clusters (GPU/TPU), and providing secure, high bandwidth optical data transport. Current energy and data systems rely on complex logistics and outdated infrastructure. Cowboy Space Corporation overcomes these challenges by enabling direct, on-demand, secure, and scalable energy distribution and data processing from space. This will revolutionize how we operate in orbit and on Earth, supporting the rapidly expanding space industrial base, ISAM (In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing) operations, remote regions, and military bases. Baiju Bhatt founded Cowboy Space Corporation in 2024. Inspired by his father’s work with NASA Langley Research Center, Baiju earned his B.S. in Physics and M.S. in Mathematics at Stanford before co-founding Robinhood, now a public company that has helped over 20 million Americans access the financial system. Cowboy Space Corporation has raised ~$365 million from Index Ventures, Interlagos, Construct Ventures, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, and others. This is an ambitious mission that demands extraordinary talent. Cowboy Space Corporation’s team has worked at places like SpaceX, Blue Origin, Stoke Space, Astranis and NASA, and is based in San Carlos, CA. If you're ready to solve complex technical challenges and help build the most important energy company in the world, we want to hear from you. ## **About the Role**: As the Stage 1 Lead, you will be the Responsible Engineer for the reusable first stage of Cowboy Space's launch vehicle, owning its entire lifecycle: from architecture and design through assembly, integrated test, launch, recovery, and refurbishment. You will serve as chief engineer, program manager, and lead systems engineer for the stage. You will lead an integrated product team of propulsion, structures, mechanical, fluids, avionics, GNC, software, and test engineers to deliver a flight-proven, rapidly reusable first stage. You will work closely with the engine, upper stage, manufacturing, test, and launch operations teams as the stage integrates with the rest of the launch system. You must be ready to stay focused, move fast, self-direct, and learn on the fly. This role reports to the Head of Launch & Propulsion. **What You’ll Do** ● Own the Stage 1 program from architecture and design through flight, recovery, and reflight ● Define Stage 1 architecture, conceptual design, and stage-level requirements in coordination with the owners of the engine, upper stage, ground systems, and other launch system elements ● Define and manage subsystem requirements and interfaces (propulsion, structures, fluids, avionics, GNC, and recovery) with subsystem owners, including the engine-to-stage interface ● Track stage technical performance, mass, margins, and risk throughout the design cycle; manage changes to requirements and interfaces and mediate technical disagreements between subsystems ● Define and manage schedule and budget for the Stage 1 program ● Lead stage assembly, integration, and integrated test campaigns (cryogenic proof, static fire) with support from manufacturing and test engineers ● Define the verification and qualification plan for stage and subsystem requirements and manage its execution ● Develop stage operating procedures and operational limits in coordination with engine, test stand, and launch operations teams ● Participate in test and launch operations to make real-time engineering decisions on technical risks ● Drive design-for-reuse decisions: recovery loads and environments, inspection intervals, life-limited parts, refurbishment procedures, and acceptance criteria for reflown stages ● Own the stage upgrade plan for improved reliability, rapid turnaround, and faster production rate; We are seeking a Junior Scheduler / Project Controls Consultant to support our growing project advisory and construction consulting practice. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career professional with hands-on experience developing and maintaining construction schedules who is looking to expand their capabilities in project controls, schedule analysis, and construction advisory. The successful candidate will ideally have approximately two years of experience working with a general contractor, construction manager, specialty contractor, or similar construction organization, with direct exposure to developing, updating, and managing construction schedules. The role will support projects across the building and infrastructure sectors and will work closely with senior schedulers, project controls professionals, project managers, and technical experts. Key Responsibilities Assist in the development, review, and maintenance of detailed construction project schedules. Develop and update Critical Path Method (CPM) schedules based on project scope, construction sequencing, and contractor work plans. Support preparation of baseline schedules, schedule updates, recovery schedules, and short-term look-ahead schedules. Review contractor schedule submissions for completeness, logic, sequencing, durations, and compliance with project requirements. Monitor project progress and incorporate actual progress into schedule updates. Identify critical and near-critical activities, schedule constraints, and potential impacts to project milestones. Assist with analysis of schedule variances and changes to the critical path. Work with project teams to collect schedule information, progress data, and supporting documentation. Assist in preparing schedule narratives, progress reports, schedule graphics, and management presentations. Support schedule impact assessments and preliminary delay analyses under the direction of senior scheduling and claims professionals. Assist with evaluating change orders and potential time impacts. Review project documentation, including drawings, specifications, contracts, progress reports, RFIs, submittals, and change documentation, to understand project sequencing and schedule impacts. Participate in project meetings and schedule review meetings with clients, contractors, designers, and other project stakeholders. Support broader project controls activities, including progress measurement, reporting, cost and schedule integration, and project performance analysis. Maintain clear and organized documentation supporting schedule updates and analyses. Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Construction Engineering, Architecture, or a related field. Approximately 2 or more years of relevant construction industry experience, preferably working for a general contractor, construction manager, or specialty contractor. Practical experience developing or maintaining construction schedules. Understanding of construction sequencing, project milestones, and the relationship between design, procurement, and construction activities. Basic understanding of Critical Path Method (CPM) scheduling principles. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to organize and analyze project information and communicate findings clearly. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Ability to work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary project team. Preferred Experience using Oracle Primavera P6. Experience with Microsoft Project or other scheduling/project controls software. Experience working on commercial buildings, healthcare, higher education, transportation, infrastructure, or other complex construction projects. Exposure to schedule review, delay analysis, change-order evaluation, or construction claims. Familiarity with construction drawings, specifications, contracts, and project documentation. Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification or interest in pursuing professional certification is a plus. Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate has started their career working directly within the construction industry and understands how projects are actually planned and built. They have had hands-on exposure to construction scheduling and are interested in developing deeper expertise in project controls, schedule analysis, and construction advisory . This position is particularly well suited to someone who has spent the first few years of their career with a contractor or construction manager and is interested in transitioning into a consulting environment where they can work across multiple projects, clients, and construction sectors. What You Will Develop In this role, you will have the opportunity to develop expertise in: Advanced CPM scheduling Primavera P6 Construction schedule review and analysis Project controls and performance reporting Schedule risk and critical path analysis Change and delay analysis Construction claims and dispute support Project advisory and owner representation You will work alongside experienced construction, engineering, scheduling, and project controls professionals and gain exposure to complex projects from both the contractor and owner perspectives. For more information, please visit Job Type: Full Time (4 days a week in office with one hybrid/ remote day) The position may be based in our Atlanta, New York, or Boston office. Some travel to project sites and client offices may be required depending on project assignments. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. role: Associate Consultant - Entry-Level Clinical Data Technology Consulting
description: Veeva’s Consultant Development Program (CDP) is an accelerated pathway that transforms early-career professionals into high-impact consultants who deliver cloud and AI solutions, helping global Life Sciences companies bring life-changing therapies to patients. ### The Role You’ll work hands-on with innovative Clinical Data Management technology, collaborating directly with internal teams and external customers to design, configure, and implement our clinical data software. In this role, you’ll learn our industry-leading clinical trial cloud platforms and work with cutting-edge AI solutions to transform how life sciences companies manage clinical trial data. Empowered from day one by a team-first culture, you will accelerate your career growth as a technical consultant who thrives in an environment where we work hard for our customers and each other. ### The Program As part of the Consultant Development Program, you will: - **Ramp up quickly:** Your journey begins with an intensive, team-based onboarding program that combines hands-on learning, transparent feedback, and active collaboration to develop the consulting skills and industry knowledge to make an impact right away. - **Learn by doing:** You won't be watching from the sidelines. You will take on real responsibility and work directly with customers to solve clinical data management problems within your first three months. - **Thrive together:** Grow alongside a supportive team of seasoned leaders and peers who actively champion your development through open communication and actionable feedback. - **Build your future:** Advance from Associate to Consultant in less than 2 years. More importantly, you’ll develop the foundation for a successful, long-term career where you can continually expand your technical expertise, lead complex projects, and evolve with our global and diverse team. ### What You'll Do As part of our Professional Services team, you are a strategic partner guiding clinical operations and data management teams through implementation. We will teach you how our CDMS software works, and you will use that knowledge to design, configure, and deliver solutions that drive real business value]. role: Avionics Embedded Software Engineer - Summer Internship 2027
description: **Advanced Reentry Technologies** **Who We Are:** Inversion is an aerospace and defense company pioneering advanced reentry technology to enable next-generation capabilities from space. By combining high-performance materials, precision aerodynamics, and mission-driven autonomy, Inversion is transforming reentry into an operational capability for an entirely new class of missions. The company’s highly maneuverable reentry spacecraft, Arc, is designed for rapid global cargo delivery, hypersonic testing, and other national security missions that require precise, controlled flight through the atmosphere. Arc creates an entirely new transportation domain, unlocking unprecedented speed and global reach. Headquartered in Los Angeles, Inversion designs, manufactures, and integrates its spacecraft under one roof, enabling the company to move rapidly from concept to flight. The company is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Spark Capital, and Lockheed Martin Ventures, with customers across the U.S. government and commercial space industry. **Position Overview:** As an Avionics Embedded Software Engineering Intern, you will support the development, integration, verification, and debugging of embedded software for Inversion’s next-generation reentry vehicles. You will sit within the Avionics team and work closely with embedded software, electrical, RF, GNC, test, and vehicle engineers to develop software that interfaces directly with flight hardware. You will gain hands-on experience developing and debugging firmware and embedded software, bringing up new hardware, integrating sensors and communications interfaces, and validating software in laboratory and hardware-in-the-loop environments. This is a practical, systems-focused internship for students interested in embedded systems, real-time software, flight computers, hardware/software integration, and aerospace applications. **Key Responsibilities:** - Work closely with embedded software and avionics engineers to develop, integrate, test, and debug flight software and firmware. - Develop software for microcontrollers, processors, sensors, communications interfaces, and other avionics hardware. - Support board bring-up and hardware/software integration, including debugging interfaces between embedded software and electrical hardware. - Implement and debug drivers and interfaces such as SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, Ethernet, GPIO, ADCs, and other embedded interfaces. - Develop and execute software tests using laboratory hardware, engineering test fixtures, and hardware-in-the-loop systems. - Support real-time software development using an RTOS or similar embedded software framework. - Debug software and hardware issues using tools such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, debuggers, serial consoles, and software instrumentation. - Develop test scripts and analysis tools using Python or similar languages to automate validation and characterize system behavior. - Support integration of sensors, flight computers, RF systems, power electronics, and other avionics subsystems. - Analyze failures and anomalies, identify root causes, and work with multidisciplinary teams to implement and verify corrective actions. - role: AUSTIN - Junior Instrumentation and Controls Engineer
location: 101 W Louis Henna Blvd, Suite 400, Austin, Texas 78728
description: Your future begins here! BGE, Inc**.** is a nationwide civil engineering consulting firm offering diverse career opportunities in a wide range of disciplines for public and private infrastructure projects. Our employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes outstanding health care, generous 401(k) match, professional career resources, and highly competitive work-life balance programs, including personal-time allowances, dependent care, and flexible Fridays. In addition, BGE provides unlimited sick leave, floating holidays, and robust career growth guidance, including organization-wide leadership and mentorship programs to help you build connections and shape your career. BGE goes beyond competitive benefits to attract and retain the best in an environment that inspires excellence. **Summary** The Junior Instrumentation and Controls Engineer is an entry level engineer who supports the delivery of instrumentation, control, and automation solutions for the energy services sector. This role assists on projects involving field instrumentation, process measurement, control narratives, PLC and DCS systems, SCADA and telemetry, safety instrumented systems, metering, control panels, and industrial networks. The Junior Instrumentation and Controls Engineer works under the direction of senior technical staff on assigned project tasks, prepares calculations and drawings for review, supports project teams and client deliverables, builds knowledge through mentorship and training, and helps deliver safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective energy solutions. **Job Responsibilities** · Assist with instrumentation and controls design and production of deliverables for energy services projects, including field instrumentation, control panels, PLC and DCS systems, SCADA, telemetry, metering, and site automation. · Prepare, under the direction of a senior engineer, instrumentation and controls design documents, including instrument index, instrument datasheets, loop diagrams, P&ID markups, wiring and termination details, panel layouts, I/O lists, and cable and conduit schedules. · Support instrument sizing and selection calculations, including flow element sizing, control valve sizing, level, pressure and temperature sizing and range setting; loop power and signal calculations, for senior review. · Learn and apply control system architecture and communication requirements, and gather information needed for protocol selection such as HART, Modbus, Profibus, Foundation Fieldbus, Ethernet/IP, and OPC, along with network layouts and remote I/O or RTU interfaces. · Draft control narratives, functional descriptions, technical reports, specifications, cost estimate backup, equipment selections, construction documents, and other project deliverables for senior engineer review. · Perform self-checks on assigned work before submittal, assist with quality control reviews at project milestones, and help verify that deliverables are complete and follow applicable ISA, NEC, NFPA, and client standards as well as project scope. · Help resolve routine design and construction-phase issues, draft responses to RFIs, review vendor submittals and instrument data for conformance with the design, and escalate unusual or complex items to a senior engineer. · Support factory acceptance testing, loop checks, point to point verification, calibration records, commissioning, and startup under supervision, including punch list tracking and as-built markups. · Communicate with internal project teams, instrument and control system vendors, and contractors on assigned tasks, and participate in client, operations, and vendor meetings alongside a senior engineer, including taking notes and tracking action items. · Build technical knowledge through mentorship, formal training, self-learning, and hands-on project and field work, ask questions when direction is unclear, and share lessons learned with peers. · Support business development and proposal efforts by compiling background information and past project data, and contribute ideas for continuous improvement of design standards, workflows, tools, templates, and checklists. **Job Requirements** · Bachelor’s degree in Electrical or Control Systems Engineering from an accredited university required. · Must have passed or be eligible to sit for the FE exam by the time of graduation. · 0 to 2 years of instrumentation and controls engineering experience. Internships, co-ops, undergraduate research, or capstone work related to process control, automation, energy services, oil and gas, power systems, or engineering consulting preferred. · Coursework-level knowledge of process measurement for flow, level, pressure, temperature, and analytical variables, along with final control elements, control loop fundamentals, and PID control. · Exposure to PLC, DCS, SCADA, HMI, safety instrumented systems, custody transfer or allocation metering, control panels, or industrial networks through coursework, internships, or student projects preferred. · Awareness of applicable codes and standards, including NFPA, IEEE, ANSI, ISA, with a willingness to learn to apply them under supervision. · Exposure to instrument sizing calculations, hazardous area classification, intrinsic safety, cause and effect development, or alarm rationalization through coursework or internships preferred. · Familiarity with design and configuration tools such as AutoCAD, AutoCAD Electrical, Revit, SmartPlant Instrumentation, MATLAB, or Python preferred. · Demonstrated ability to follow technical direction, organize assigned work, manage deadlines on multiple tasks, and communicate clearly in writing and in person with team members, vendors, and project stakeholders, including in plant and field environments. · Strong analytical, problem-solving, attention to detail, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills, with a commitment to accuracy and to learning quickly. Some of our Benefits: - 401k Match: 100% up to 4% of your contributions with immediate vesting + 3% Safe Harbor Contribution with immediate vesting - Merit-Based Bonus Compensation - Medical, Dental, Vision Insurance; BGE contributes to HSA on eligible plans - 9 paid Holidays, including 3 Floating holidays - Personal Time Allowances - 2 to 4 weeks of Vacation, depending on experience-level. Unused vacation carries over to the next year. - "Unlimited" Sick Days. - Mentorship Program – Provides you with the opportunity to learn and receive guidance from seasoned professionals. - Employee Referral Program that pays you for bringing great people into the BGE family BGE is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We prohibit discrimination and all employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, Vietnam Era Veteran Status, Disabled Veteran Status, or any other classification protected by federal, state or local laws. NO SPONSORSHIP NO AGENCIES

The Civil Engineering Department of AECOM’s Transportation Business Line is actively seeking an Entry-Level Civil/Highway Engineer to be based in our Newark, DE office. Under the supervision of a Project Engineer, the appropriately qualified applicant will be part of a design team responsible for designing small to large-scale highway projects such as roadway rehabilitation/safety improvement projects, intersection improvements/optimizations, and interstate/limited access highway widening/reconstruction. Design responsibilities include horizontal/vertical geometry, pavement design, 3D modeling, intersections/interchanges design, traffic control/staging, signing and pavement markings design, ADA, Pedestrian and Bicycle design, etc. Current notable projects include Airport Road Extension in Rehoboth Beach, DE; SR 1 and Cave Neck Road Grade Separated Interchange in Milton, DE; and SR 5 and Harmons Hill Road Intersection Improvements in Millsboro, DE. The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to: Obtaining and reviewing existing information including some field work/site investigations. Originating technical calculations that advance the design of the project. Assisting in the development of roadway construction, intersection grading, traffic control, and signing and pavement marking. Developing 3D models using civil engineering software such as Bentley OpenRoads Designer or Autodesk Civil 3D. Assisting in the preparation of technical reports and project specifications Performs work under supervision in accordance with agreed-upon budget and schedule. Previous work experience or internship with engineering firms, contractors, or DOTs involved in highway design, construction, management, or other transportation-related projects.
