We’re an all-in-one financial services platform that brings together banking, high-yield savings, credit cards, point-of-sale lending, investing, and crypto in one place. We also partner with employers, HCM providers, gig platforms, and others to deliver embedded financial services to millions of employees and frontline workers. We’re backed by Walmart, the world’s largest retailer, and Ribbit Capital, one of fintech’s most respected investors, giving us rare scale, distribution, and the opportunity to build something truly category-defining. But what really sets OnePay apart is how we move. Our customers don’t have time to wait… and neither do we. This place moves fast, and we’re looking for people who are: - Ready to run - Hungry and driven by urgency - Exceptional at what they do, with low ego - Comfortable operating in motion # The Role As an AI Research Intern, your mandate is to research and prototype foundation models, both transformer-based and graph-based, applied to OnePay's customer, transaction, and merchant data. You'll work on real modeling problems and build a working prototype that demonstrates the approach. This role will impact OnePay's vision by providing a remarkable customer experience, driving positive business outcomes, and improving operational efficiency. You will work closely with the product, engineering and applied science team(s) working across all business units. This role reports to the Head of AI/ML. This role is responsible for: - Research, design, and train foundation models on OnePay's data, working with transformer and/or graph-based architectures. - Run experiments, evaluate results rigorously, and turn promising findings into a working prototype. - Opportunity to work in an extremely fast paced growing company - Partner with Product, Engineering and Analytics teams to ensure we are providing a remarkable customer experience. - Driving significant impact on the company’s bottom line. # You Bring - **Final-Year Graduate Student:** You’re in the final year of a master’s or PhD program, expected to graduate in Fall 2027 or Spring 2028, majoring in Engineering or a related field. - **Deep Learning Fundamentals:** You have a strong grasp of how neural networks work under the hood, including backpropagation, attention, embeddings, optimization, and training dynamics. You've implemented, trained, or fine-tuned models yourself through research, coursework, or personal projects, and you're comfortable working in PyTorch or an equivalent framework. - **Prior Experience:** You've completed at least one previous internship in research, machine learning, or software engineering, or have built substantial personal or academic projects you're excited to talk through. - **Availability:** This is a full-time, 8-week program running June 21 - August 13, 2027. You are available to work in our New York City office at least 3-4 days a week throughout. - **Proactive & Collaborative Attitude:** You have an act-like-an-owner mentality, thrive in a fast-moving environment, and enjoy working with others to achieve collective goals. - **Critical Thinking & Problem-Solving Skills:** You enjoy tackling complex challenges, analyzing problems, and developing solutions. Clear communication of ideas is one of your strengths. - **Organized & Detail-Oriented:** You’re a keen listener with strong organizational skills, capable of managing multiple tasks efficiently. - **Excited to Learn & Grow:** You are passionate about being part of a rapidly growing start-up and look forward to expanding your skills in a real-world setting. ## Nice to Have - Familiarity with transformer-based foundation model architectures, including pre-training, fine-tuning, inference, and the tradeoffs between approaches. - Exposure to graph-based learning or graph foundation models, such as GNNs, message passing, or representation learning on graph-structured data. - Coursework or projects involving Large Language Models or Generative AI. - Research output in any of the above: publications, workshop papers, or open-source contributions. # What We Offer - Early access to a high potential, high growth fintech - Hands on experience building product ready to ship - Beautiful NYC SoHo Office - Professional development and team social outings # Program & Application Timeline - Program runs June 21 - August 13, 2027 (8 weeks, full-time, in our NYC office) - We review applications and conduct interviews on a rolling basis as they come in - No offer decisions will be made until the application window closes – all candidates are evaluated together before final decisions go out - We are targeting a finalized cohort by December 1, 2026 - If there are intern spots still available, we may reopen applications in Spring 2027 **Work Authorization:** OnePay will not sponsor applicants who need employment sponsored visas for this position. Future sponsorship will not be considered. # Standard Interview Process Our process varies by role. Most candidates go through: - AI-assisted initial screen - Interview with Talent Partner - Technical or Hiring Manager Interview - Team Interview - Executive Interview - Offer! # Equal Employment Opportunity To build technology and products that are used and loved by people and solve real-world problems, we need to build a team with many different perspectives and experiences. We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply. Applicants in need of special assistance or accommodation during the interview process or in accessing our website may contact us at .

Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. #### Assembly, Integration and Test Intern (Winter 2027) Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks, and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on challenging projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed and tested hardware/software that is heading to space on our first satellite, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis. If you have already graduated from a four-year university, please apply to be an Associate Engineer. #### Role - Work on an interdisiciplinary team to design, build, and test satellite hardware and software. - Work with the Electrical, Mechanical, RF, Propulsion engineering teams to develop assembly and integration test plans and procedures based on concepts and designs - Learn to use various pieces of test equipment and instruments (thermal chambers, vibration tables, DAQs, oscilloscopes, etc.) to successfully execute test plans. - Coordinate assembly, integration and environmental test efforts #### Requirements - Currently pursuing a four-year degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering (or equivalent technical degree) - A passion for hardware development, including working in a fast-paced environment and hands-on design and development - Ability to handle multiple tasks and prioritize - Strong communication skills - Familiarity with spacecraft systems and operation - Must be onsite 5 days a week #### Bonus - Hands-on experience in designing, building, and testing - Experience writing Python code to: Interface with test equipment, process large datasets, visualize data - Experience in CAD - Direct electrical or mechanical design experience - Demonstrated ability to debug hardware and software problems under time pressure The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour. Base Hourly Pay $29—$29 USD **U.S. Citizenship, Lawful Permanent Residency, or Refugee/Asylee Status Required** (To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States, or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)) Our mission and products are built for everyone, regardless of gender, race, creed, or background. ### **Company Introduction** At Bot Auto, we are revolutionizing the transportation of goods with our cutting-edge autonomous trucks, enhancing the quality of life for communities around the globe. With the agility of a start-up and the wisdom of seasoned experts, Bot Auto boasts a team that has achieved numerous world-firsts and unparalleled innovations. United by a shared vision, we create miracles and propel the future of transportation. Join us and transform your dreams into reality. ### **About the Role** We are seeking a motivated **IT Specialist Intern** to join our team and gain hands-on experience across corporate IT operations. This role focuses on the day-to-day work that keeps IT running — user onboarding and offboarding, asset management, and frontline support — while building exposure to enterprise tooling, monitoring, and automation. You will work alongside experienced engineers who will mentor you on real infrastructure in a fast-moving environment. The ideal candidate is eager to learn, detail-oriented, and ready to take ownership of tasks that directly support the team. ### Key Responsibilities - Execute user onboarding and offboarding workflows — account provisioning, hardware setup, and access removal - Manage IT asset inventory — track, tag, and audit laptops, peripherals, and equipment throughout their lifecycle - Image, deploy, and prepare laptops and workstations for new hires and replacements - Maintain stock of IT supplies and peripherals; monitor levels and coordinate reorders - Respond to help desk tickets and provide frontline support for common hardware, software, and access issues - Assist with monitoring and alerting — triage alerts, escalate issues, and help maintain dashboards - Support patching and software deployment tasks under engineer guidance - Maintain and improve IT documentation — runbooks, how-to guides, and inventory records - Assist with office IT logistics: conference room AV, desk setups, and equipment moves ### **Qualifications** **Required:** - Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in IT, computer science, or a related field — or equivalent self-taught/certification path (A+, Network+) - Basic understanding of operating systems (Windows and macOS) and common productivity tools - Strong organizational skills and attention to detail - Clear written and verbal communication; comfortable helping non-technical users - Ability to lift and move IT equipment as needed **Preferred:** - Exposure to ticketing/ITSM systems - Familiarity with scripting basics (Python, PowerShell, or Bash) - Interest in networking, identity management, or infrastructure automation - Prior customer service or help desk experience

***“In 36 months, agentic AI systems will be an operating reality across major institutions. We intend to be central to it.” — Dr. Jim Rebesco, Cofounder and CEO, Striveworks*** The government’s demand for AI is growing far faster than the systems required to support it. Fewer than 15% of federal AI programs have reached sustained production, despite billions of dollars invested. The models perform in testing, but they degrade in the real world. And when performance drops, trust goes with it. Striveworks was built to solve that problem. ## **What you’ll build** Since 2018, we have delivered the most trusted AI systems operating in real-world use cases—providing a layer of assurance underneath hundreds of deployed models that monitors performance, manages drift, and sustains systems long after they leave the lab. As a Junior Quality Engineer, you will be challenged—and trusted—on day one to safeguard and improve the quality of our core products. In this mission-critical work, you will verify that software is performing as designed, document test results and implications, plan and implement new test strategies, and grow in your knowledge of our software. You’re right for this opportunity if you value and possess technical aptitude and enjoy pushing the boundaries of your own capabilities. You are passionate about what is possible with software engineering, data science, and machine learning. You are comfortable following a defined plan while also thinking about how it can be improved, and you communicate results and ideas to your team throughout the process. ## **What it’s like here** We lead with trust, treat each other with respect, and use candor consistently, kindly, and constructively. We care deeply about our work, and we find genuine satisfaction in doing it well. Above all, we take ownership—because we feel the weight of collective results personally. We are looking for people who share these values and are eager to put them into practice. ## **What we’re looking for** - A bachelor’s degree in computer science or another engineering or science discipline, or completion of a software development boot camp and 0–2 years of relevant professional experience - Understanding of core programming concepts and basic proficiency in one or more programming languages - Understanding of software testing concepts and methodology - Strong problem solving and analytical skills - Attention to detail - Ability to clearly communicate technical topics in documents and conversations - US citizenship and eligibility and willingness to obtain and maintain a US security clearance (Secret or above) The following isn’t required, but we’d love to see it: - Proficiency with test automation tools such as Selenium, Cypress, Playwright, TestRail, React Testing Library, Postman, or similar - Exposure to or proficiency with modern software engineering tools and processes (Agile, version control, issue tracking, CI/CD, etc.) - Proficiency in JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, or Golang - Experience using SQL and working with relational databases such as PostgreSQL - Experience with containerization tools such as Docker, Podman, or Kubernetes (K8s) - Exposure to concepts in machine learning and data science, and/or machine learning libraries like TensorFlow, PyTorch, sklearn, or similar - Experience delivering technology solutions in secure government environments - Active Secret (or above) US security clearance This position offers a hybrid/on-site work environment at our office in Austin, TX. ## **Compensation** The anticipated base pay range for this position is $85,000–$100,000/year. Striveworks’ total compensation package includes a competitive base salary, equity grants, and cash bonuses. ## **Benefits include:** - Medical/dental/vision insurance - Voluntary life, long-term disability, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance - HSA and FSA (including dependent care FSA) plans - 401(k) plan - Unlimited PTO - Paid parental leave **Ready to build systems that work for a mission that matters? description: About the role At Rippling, Engineering is at the heart of our business and culture. We believe in our early talent’s potential, experience and aspirations. Our mission is to open the realm of possibilities and opportunities for students by fostering growth through mentorship and training, ownership through impactful and innovative projects, and, of course, fun through our diverse culture and work hard, play harder attitude. As an Engineering Intern, you will join one of our many teams in Summer 2027 (May/June - August/September) to develop robust, well-designed products, implement new updates and features, and solve complex problems that affect our business and our clients. Rippling Interns gain the experience of full-time engineers with responsibilities, ownership, and opportunity. Interns will be assigned projects that not only have an impact on the business, but that are also scoped to fit within the time constraints of their internship so they can see the full impact of their work. We provide our interns exciting and innovative projects to work on that allow them to see the fruition of their work. During your 13 weeks at Rippling, we will provide all of the tools needed to be successful. Your dedicated mentor and manager will provide support for your learning and development throughout your time with us. You will join your fellow interns in a variety of socials, talks with Rippling leaders, and more! What you will do Utilize your software engineering experience to tackle important projects, solving problems, and developing quality code Think critically and apply your knowledge to real world, complex problems Actively participate in team meetings to scope, drive, and progress your projects Learn about the business, our clients’ needs, and the impact of your team and related projects Attend Meet & Greets with various executives and teams to gain a holistic view of what it takes to run a company like Rippling Foster relationships with your intern cohort and teams through both exclusive internship social events and company/office-wide events What you will need Previous internship/Co-op experience in software engineering utilizing Python Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master's degree in computer science or in a related field graduating after the internship's completion Excellent communication skills to work cross functionally and across departments Solid programming skills with an emphasis on backend experience and knowledge Ability to adapt and ask action-oriented questions to progress Passion and drive to constantly learn and develop your engineering skills Even if you don’t meet all of the requirements listed here, we still encourage you to apply. Skills can be used in lots of different ways and your life and professional experience may be relevant beyond what our list of requirements has outlined. About the team Here at Rippling, we have many teams that span across all different types of work varying from product development to platform enhancement. Our various product teams have a combination of both directly user-facing products as well as interfaces for other engineering teams. There are challenges for the team that range from building for usability to scaling for massive growth and a wide array of engineering requirements. Rippling’s platform engineering teams provide a layer of abstractions for every product team to build quickly and scale effortlessly. Providing a strong platform layer enables Rippling to build as a startup of startups. These teams are responsible for building the foundational software that powers the Rippling platform. Additional Information Rippling is an equal opportunity employer. Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets. We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together. **Role description:** We are currently searching for a Water Engineer to support our team in Middletown, CT. We are looking for dedicated, creative, and energetic candidates interested in tackling challenges and developing sustainable solutions to address water issues. Collaborating with our experienced water professionals, you will support and drive the development of projects, interact, and work with clients, and develop your technical capabilities. **Role accountabilities:** The Water Engineer will possess a strong foundation in engineering concepts and theories related to water, wastewater, and stormwater management. You will need to have excellent technical aptitude and be familiar with various software tools such as CAD, AutoCAD, Revit, HEC-RAS, HEC-HMS, SWMM, EPANET, and Modflow, which are beneficial for project work. You will need to be skilled in evaluating, planning, designing, and supporting the management of projects involving water treatment, wastewater treatment, and stormwater conveyance including pipelines and pumping facilities. Additionally, you will need to provide valuable support in project management efforts including managing project scopes, budgets, and client deliverables. As part of our team, you will engage in the full cycle of sustainability and resilience project management, from assessment and development to ongoing support. You will exercise judgement when working on engineering tasks, including making critical decisions on project details and selecting suitable engineering solutions. Fieldwork duties are also crucial, involving activities like site visits, water quality analysis, construction inspection, sampling, water quality analyses, flow monitoring set-up, and monitoring technology evaluations, plant operations information, process troubleshooting, and optimization. Additionally, you will support asset management projects by conducting data analytics, performance evaluations, and assessments to optimize performance of water/wastewater/stormwater facilities. Your work will also include preparing various reports and materials, participating in client meetings, and utilizing digital tools to boost collaboration and enhance project delivery such as SharePoint, BIM, PowerBI, and Augmented Reality, as well as designing and managing databases and cloud-based computing services. **Qualifications & Experience:** Required Qualifications: - A Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering (or a closely related engineering discipline) Preferred Qualifications: - Prior work/internship experience at a design or consulting engineering firm or municipal work environment. - Familiarity/ experience with CAD, AutoCAD, Revit. You will contribute to meaningful projects throughout the product lifecycle, from design and implementation through testing and production deployment. You will work alongside experienced engineers who are invested in your growth. You will gain practical experience building cloud services, solving distributed-systems problems, and understanding how production software is developed, operated, and improved. ## What You’ll Do - Develop features and services that support the lifecycle of customer workspaces and databases - Build automation for provisioning, scaling, upgrades, backups, and recovery - Improve service reliability, availability, observability, and operational efficiency - Design and implement backend services and APIs for cloud database management - Investigate and resolve performance, scalability, and correctness issues - Write production code, tests, documentation, and technical designs - Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, debugging, and team planning - Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and cross-functional partners Depending on your team and project, you may work on areas such as control-plane services, data-plane systems, cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, developer tooling, monitoring, or customer-facing cloud experiences. ## Required Qualifications - Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s degree program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field - Strong foundation in data structures, algorithms, and software design - Programming experience in Go, Java, Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, or a similar language - Understanding of operating systems, distributed systems, networking, or databases - Familiarity with Linux or Unix-based systems - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills - Ability to communicate clearly and collaborate effectively with teammates - Curiosity, ownership, and willingness to learn Prior professional experience is not required. We welcome candidates who have developed their skills through coursework, research, projects, internships, or open-source contributions. ## Preferred Qualifications - Coursework or project experience in distributed systems, cloud computing, databases, networking, or operating systems - Experience building backend services, APIs, automation, or developer tools - Familiarity with containers, Kubernetes, or public cloud platforms - Experience with observability, monitoring, debugging, or performance analysis - Experience contributing to production software or substantial technical projects - Interest in reliability engineering and operating services at scale ## What You’ll Gain - Hands-on experience building cloud software for a production database platform - Mentorship from experienced cloud and distributed-systems engineers - Exposure to cloud infrastructure, database systems, reliability, and large-scale automation - Opportunities to own meaningful work and see your contributions move toward production - Collaboration with teams across engineering and product - A supportive environment focused on technical growth and meaningful ownership

### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. ### **About the Flight Test Engineering Team** Zipline’s **Flight Test Engineering** team is a specialized group that designs flight test courses and methods to support our overall system validation progress. This involves developing custom flight control software for complex maneuvers and collaborating with development engineers to design rigorous tests for all critical edge cases. We leverage expertise in system design, statistics, flight physics, and sound experimental methods to ensure our flight tests are effective and safe. The team partners closely with Controls and Dynamics, Embedded Software, Autonomy, Systems Engineering, Powertrain, Structure, and Flight Operations teams to build comprehensive test plans and test cards. Our work spans simulation, hardware testing, data-driven analysis, and system-level evaluations that support deployments across the globe. As an intern, you’ll collaborate with engineers across these domains, gaining hands-on exposure to how industry-leading autonomous systems are designed, tested, and validated at scale. ### **The Role** As a Flight Test Engineering Intern, you will be instrumental in analyzing flight test data logs to determine test effectiveness, identify success/failure root causes, and track performance trends. You will also directly contribute to the design of new flight test campaigns, collaborating with other engineers to define the test scope, test method, and data post-processing. This is a unique opportunity for someone excited to learn how complex robotic systems are validated, who enjoys problem-solving, and who wants to build real-world experience working with autonomy software, data analysis, and systems engineering. ### **What You'll Do** - Analyze flight test data logs using custom scripts (Python, DataBricks, SQL) to identify anomalies, assess reliability, track performance trends, and perform regression analyses. - Design, oversee the execution, and review the results of software validation and flight test campaigns to ensure new features perform as intended and prevent hardware/software regression. - Daily test and monitor the develop branch to quickly surface instability and potential future issues. - Collaborate with cross-functional partners (GNC, Aerodynamics, Structures, Systems Engineering) to ensure system-level requirements (e.g., acceleration, range, climb rate) are clear, measurable, and that vehicle changes are mature for flight testing. - Define or develop novel test infrastructure, including application-based tools to support flight testing, new instrumentation systems (e.g., load cells, vision systems). or modified flight control software, to collect auxiliary data in flight. - Establish and maintain documentation, dashboards, and SQL search queries to track test progress and operational efficiency. - Be ready to directly own any aspect of flight operations (preflight, launch, flight maneuvers, incident reporting) or supervise these activities with the flight operations team. ### **What You'll Bring** - You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies in physics, mathematics, mechanical, aerospace, system engineering, computer science, electrical engineering or related fields. Masters and PhD students are also eligible. - Strong mathematical and physics background. - Experience in autonomous vehicle/ robotic system integration and testing work. - Experience in data process, visualization. - Strong written and verbal communication skills. ### **What Else You Should Know** *This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April/May.* Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Our 13,000+ people are united in a shared purpose to pursue the limitless potential of technology and ingenuity for clients across defense, national security, public safety, civilian, and military health organizations. Join Accenture Federal Services, a technology company within global Accenture. Recognized as a Glassdoor Top 100 Best Place to Work, we offer a collaborative and caring community where you feel like you belong and are empowered to grow, learn and thrive through hands-on experience, certifications, industry training and more. **About the APX Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) Program:** APX (Advanced Partnership Accelerator) is a Center of Excellence under AFS’ Data & AI capability. The APX Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) Program represents a strategic initiative to position Accenture Federal Services at the forefront of artificial intelligence innovation in government. This program embeds top technical talent directly with federal clients to fast track the adoption and implementation of advanced technologies from Palantir, Databricks, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and cutting edge AI partners. As an FDE, you will serve as the critical bridge between breakthrough AI technology and mission-critical federal requirements. You'll work hands-on with the most advanced AI models available, translating their transformative potential into tangible value for defense, intelligence, civilian, and public health missions. This is not a traditional consulting role; FDEs are technical practitioners, innovators, and trusted advisors who operate at the cutting edge of what's possible with AI in highly regulated, high-security federal environments. **What You Will Do:** The APX FDE program exists because federal missions cannot wait for slow, siloed development cycles. They need embedded engineers who move with urgency, autonomy, and precision while being able to reach back to broader support across AFS. As a Junior FDE, you will work at the intersection of engineering, product thinking and client delivery, helping technical teams move from ambiguous client problems, to working proof-of-concept, to production-grade deployment in a matter of weeks. In this role you will: - Embed within client environments as part of a forward deployed engineering (FDE) team to build rapid prototypes using AI tools, coding assistants, and modern frameworks - Use AI tools (LLMs, coding assistants, agentic frameworks) as part of daily development work - Support integration of solutions into complex client environments, including legacy systems and regulated data contexts - Work across the tech stack (frontend, backend, APIs, simple data pipelines) and help develop applications and workflows that use structured and unstructured enterprise data - Assist in evaluating model outputs, testing workflows, and applying responsible AI guardrails - Implement AI solutions such as RAG workflows, semantic search, prompt engineering patterns, and simple agent behaviors - Work with senior FDEs to clarify problem statements and translate them into technical plans - Participate in rapid experimentation cycles and incorporate user feedback into updates, documenting solution decisions and contributing to internal learning assets - Leverage technical expertise to help clients navigate the rapidly evolving technological landscape, serving as a trusted advisor on emerging AI capabilities, increasing user adoption and scaling mission impact - Share observations, user friction points, reusable assets and field intelligence back to APX teams to improve delivery approaches **What You Bring:** - **Mission-first Mindset & Relentless Problem Solving:** You move fast because the mission can’t wait. You make smart bets in ambiguous terrain, taking ownership early and giving every challenge your full drive before ever considering stepping back. You push through ambiguity, communicate risks and trade-offs, investigate solutions independently to forge the future, and maintain momentum even when the path forward is unclear. - **Grit & Tenacity to Engineer at the Edge**: You remain steady when projects get messy and keep pushing forward through rapid experimentation cycles. You show up confidently in client working sessions, support senior FDEs at the mission edge, adapt in real time, and help teams operate decisively even in uncertainty. - **Bias for Building:** You iterate quickly, communicate plainly across technical and non-technical teammates, ask sharp questions, and summarize decisions in a way that moves teams forward with confidence and alignment. You build work that adds value for our clients, making bold ideas happen fast. - **Limitless Curiosity & Frontier Learning:** You learn rapidly across a wide, rapidly changing technical frontier, from LLMs and agent frameworks to cloud platforms and enterprise AI ecosystems. You approach new tools with curiosity, adaptability, and velocity, and you prefer building and testing over long specification cycles. **Here’s What You Need:** - Bachelor’s Degree or demonstrated hands-on coding experience building and shipping software projects - Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Python, R, Rust) with knowledge of building production services - Familiarity with Generative AI (LLMs, chatbots, or AI-powered apps) and eagerness to learn how model outputs influence product workflows - Exposure working with APIs and simple data flows, managing structured and unstructured data and ensure data quality. - Ability to travel, dependent on client and team - Must be a U.S. Citizen and ability to obtain a federal security clearance **Bonus Points if You Have:** - Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Economics, Statistics, or a related technical field - Experience with Palantir, Databricks, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or other emerging technology platforms - Prior client experience or collaborative technical work (consulting internships, hackathons, customer success engineering, or team-based builds) - Exposure to cloud services (AWS, Azure, GCP) from coursework, certificates, internships, or individual projects - Experience integrating or deploying code in environments with constraints (legacy systems, governance, access controls) - Demonstrated ability to take a small idea from zero-to-prototype independently

By the end of your internship, you will have the skills and knowledge to produce your own shows, setting you on the path to a successful career in event production. The Event Producer Intern is responsible for entertaining and informing fans with Daktronics and other audio/video equipment for videoboard shows and will work on-site at James Madison University (JMU) in Harrisonburg, VA. As an Event Production Intern at James Madison University (JMU), your work will closely mirror the responsibilities and tasks performed by a full-time Event Producer. You will play an integral role in producing cohesive and professional game day productions for JMU's athletic teams at various venues. Learn about Daktronics control systems, live video production equipment, and stats integration software to effectively operate and manage the technical aspect of game day production. During live events, assist in producing and directing the show for the videoboard. This involves communicating effectively with the production crew and the athletics event manager to ensure seamless production. Learn how to plan and produce game-day video roll-ins, highlight packages, and other video element for use during live event. This includes creating and organizing content to enhance the fan experience. Assist in the supervision, scheduling, and development of the game-day production crew for all sports. Join professional meetings with the fulltime Event Production to learn how to collaborate with JMU staff to develop game day scripts. Attend on-site meetings with event producer to learn how an event producer engages with advertisers, Marketing to ensure that event production meets the expectations and goals of all stakeholders. Efficiently manage, organize, and execute non-contractual events within the basketball arena and football stadium. Develop, update, and render content using predefined templates like matchup graphics, upcoming event graphics, stat backgrounds, and prompt graphics. Utilize Photoshop skills to create cutout photos for graphics, especially for headshot and senior day graphics. Contribute to game-week preparations by loading and testing content on machines, updating content buttons, and more. When necessary, assume gameday video board crew roles such as graphics operation, replay operation, camera operation, directing/technical directing. Schedule content for various displays during events and smaller ad hoc requirements. Manage content scripts, creation lists, sponsorship reports, and other content-related needs. Travel to other sites to perform Event Production duties as needed. Contribute to Daktronics Intern Group: Recruiting events (if applicable). Give internship capstone presentation and attend colleagues’ presentations. Build and maintain professional relationships. A unique aspect of this position is not only being able to technically work with these systems but developing an eye for what looks good on a display. Throughout your internship, you will gain valuable experience in the field of event production, honing your skills and contributing to the delivery of high-quality, engaging game-day productions for JMU's athletic events. This hands-on experience will prepare you for a future career in event production and offer a comprehensive understanding of the industry's inner workings. When will I work? The actual offer will consider a wide range of factors, including relevant education, experiences, location, and applicable local legislation. This position is eligible for a subset of our company benefits including employee discount program, employee assistance program, community donation program, unpaid time off, 401(k), Employee Stock Purchase Plan, leaves, disability and accommodations. Qualifications To be considered for JMU Event Production Intern, we require the following: Academic Requirements: Preferred applicants will be full-time students currently enrolled in an accredited Bachelor's degree program related to Broadcast Engineering, Graphic Design, Communications, Video Production, or other related degree. Candidate must be enrolled as a student and registered for at least 12 credits (undergraduate) or 9 credits (graduate) at the time of application. Will consider December 2025 and May 2026 graduates. Overtime will be required, as needed, to support special events and travel. Unofficial transcripts or web transcripts must be submitted with application. Travel Requirements: Willing to travel up to 10% of the time on trips ranging in length from two days to two weeks, including some weekends. This requirement will be verified through a motor vehicle record (MVR) check conducted in accordance with applicable federal, state, provincial, and local laws. Other Requirements: You can quickly learn technical product features and functions and can communicate to non-technical customers and users. Can capture and evaluate non-technical customer feedback and organize to communicate to technical product managers and developers. You have a strong interest in sports and can relate to stakeholders of sporting applications. You’re an outgoing, self-motivated, flexible, well-organized person who is both empathetic and personable. You understand customers, so know the work schedule may include evenings and weekends. Strong customer service orientation, excellent communication, attentive listening, and interpersonal proficiency. Collaborative team player with a positive attitude. As an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on challenging projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed and tested hardware/software that is currently in space or heading to space shortly on on of our satellites, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis. If you have already graduated from a four-year university, please apply to be an Associate Engineer. #### Role - Work on an interdisciplinary team to design, build, and test satellite hardware and software. - Operate and setup environmental test equipment including: - Ambient thermal chambers - Thermal Vacuum Chambers (TVAC) - Vibration shaker tables - EMI/EMC test equipment - Learn to use various pieces of test equipment and instruments (thermal chambers, vibration tables, DAQs, oscilloscopes, etc.) to successfully execute test plans. - Set up, operate, and conduct environmental testing including vibration, acoustics, thermal, thermal vacuum, RF #### Requirements - Have a four-year degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering (or equivalent technical degree) - A passion for hardware development, including working in a fast-paced environment and hands-on design and development - Ability to handle multiple tasks and prioritize time effectively - Strong communication skills - Familiarity with spacecraft systems and operation - Must be onsite 5 days a week #### Bonus - Hands-on experience in designing, building, and testing - Experience writing Python code to: Interface with test equipment, process large datasets, visualize data - Experience in CAD - Direct electrical or mechanical design experience - Demonstrated ability to debug hardware and software problems under time pressure The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour. Your responsibilities will include: - **Quantitative Models and Solutions:** You'll build models and create innovative data-based solutions for clients using programming languages, such as R, Python, Stata, SAS, Excel, and VBA (e.g. conducting data and statistical analysis, econometric analysis, building interactive dashboards, etc.). - **Qualitative Research and Literature Review:** You'll conduct comprehensive research, including market analysis, literature reviews, document examination, and writing memos to provide insights and support expert reports. - **Supporting Expert Witnesses:** You'll assist in preparing expert reports and presentations, helping our experts present complex economic and financial concepts clearly in legal and regulatory contexts. - **Collaborating with Team Members:** Effective communication and teamwork are critical. You will work in a collaborative atmosphere where dedication to project success and individual career and professional development are emphasized. You will have the opportunity to discover where your strengths and interests lie and how you can best apply your skills. The work environment is collegial; and there is significant, on-going contact between senior and junior staff. **The Candidate** The ideal candidates will be pursuing, and possess: - An undergraduate degree in a quantitative discipline (e.g. economics, computer science, data science, and mathematics), with strong academic performance. Successful applicants typically have a GPA of 3.7 or higher (based on a 4.0 scale). - Great teamwork and leadership skills. Our project work is done almost exclusively on teams, so it’s critical that our interns work well with others. - Intellectual curiosity and creativity. We are looking for candidates who consistently want to learn more and approach problems with creativity. - A high degree of ownership and commitment. Successful interns are committed to delivering their best work product, taking ownership of their work, and engaging in excellent client services. - Strong communication skills. **To Be Considered for the Research Analyst Intern Position:** Please submit the following materials as soon as possible via the application below. - Cover Letter - Resume - Transcript(s) (unofficial copies accepted) *To streamline the process, please use your school-issued email address on your application.* *The anticipated base gross salary for this position in Washington DC is $1,850.00 per week.* **EQUAL OPPORTUNITY** The Brattle Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. description: **About Us** At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. **About the Summer Internship Program** Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: **Cohort #1** Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 **Cohort #2** Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at our Torrance headquarters and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package. **About the Role** As a Space Mechanical Design Intern, you will contribute to the mechanical design and development of Antares reactor and power systems, with a particular focus on space applications. You will work on hardware ranging from space radiators and power conversion components to reactor mechanical systems, taking projects from early design and manufacturing concepts through integration and testing. You will also evaluate how Antares systems could be deployed across different applications, translating customer operating conditions into technical requirements and concepts of operation. This role offers exposure to both detailed hardware development and the system-level engineering required to deploy nuclear power systems in space and terrestrial applications. **Roles and Responsibilities:** - Design, develop, and test space radiator hardware - Develop manufacturing approaches for scaling radiator technology from small test coupons to full-scale hardware - Contribute to the development and integration of space power conversion systems - Own the design and development of power conversion components such as recuperators, primary heat exchangers, and piping - Support overall mechanical integration of space power conversion systems - Contribute to reactor mechanical design - Perform microgrid analyses, including identifying nominal customer load profiles, outage frequencies, integration with other energy sources, and power distribution requirements - Develop reactor deployment assessments and concepts of operation for candidate applications - Evaluate external markets, including process heat, to identify potential reactor deployment concepts and customer use cases - Translate potential customer applications into technical requirements - Expand technoeconomic analyses to evaluate potential reactor applications and deployment scenarios **Basic Qualifications:** - Enrolled in at least a bachelor’s degree program, and going into your Junior or Senior year of studies - Must have prior internship experience, or significant (>1yr) project team, laboratory, or research experience **Preferred Skills & Experience:** - GPA of 3.5 or above - Experience in a University club or organization, leadership role preferred - Strong interpersonal and technical communication skills (examples: leading a student project team, presenting research at conferences, etc.) - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail - Ability to work cross-departmentally with different groups and teams - Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements - Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively **Location** - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises. **Culture** At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - *Think in Systems* - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - *Obsess over the End User* - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - *Be Unconstrained by Convention* - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - *Go Where the Work I*s - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - *Operate in the Grey* - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption **Equal Opportunity** Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. The Reliability & Maintenance Engineering (RME) team are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all the robotics and material handling equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey! About the Role: The Automation Engineering Apprentice(ship) (AEA) will learn to focus on equipment troubleshooting and maintaining material handling equipment (MHE) such as conveyors, sortation systems, scanners, cameras, print and apply labeling systems, scales, HMI systems, and control cabinets. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of this role is to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement. Amazon AEA apprentices are engaged in the assembly and maintenance of complex machines, plants, and systems in the Reliability & Maintenance Engineering sector or in organizations which purchase and operate such mechatronic systems. Apprentices are paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. They are expected to work based on technical documents and instructions and carry out their work in compliance with the relevant provisions and safety regulations. The successful candidate is an effective communicator, works well in a team, and is self-motivated. They should have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate their activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. In addition to developing your skills, you will be mentored by senior technicians to grow in your role. Key job responsibilities Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to: You will conduct preventative/corrective maintenance and basic troubleshooting of robotics and robotic work cells You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all material handling equipment components You will maintain and troubleshoot motors, photo eyes, relays, proximity sensors, solenoids, motor starters, tachs, etc. You will assist with basic electronics/Programmable Logic Controllers troubleshooting You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head

description: ISW Internship Program Overview ISW is offering in-person, remote, and hybrid internships for Spring 2027. Instructions to apply for the scholarship are below. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) is committed to training the next generation of national security leaders through its innovative educational programs. ISW seeks motivated and experienced college students or recent graduates to join our intern team. ISW offers internships across diverse research portfolios and departments, including Russia, China, and Iran's proxy networks. ISW also offers internships in Geospatial Intelligence and Technologies, National Security and lntelligence Analysis, and our Cognitive Warfare Task Force. Why Work for ISW? ISW believes that ground realities must drive the formulation of strategy and policy. In pursuit of this principle, ISW conducts detailed open-source intelligence analysis to provide timely and accurate information on current conflicts and security threats directly to policymakers and warfighters. Interns at ISW have an unparalleled opportunity to analyze conflicts in ways that directly inform policy-makers on some of the most pressing issues facing American national security. Our interns work directly with analysts. They receive classroom education, regular leadership engagement, and a chance to work with cutting-edge technologies employed in business and the intelligence community. Interns have the opportunity to stand at the front lines of military research and policy development, tackling the latest crises in the headlines. The ISW Internship Program is one of three core education programs housed within The General David H. Petraeus Center for Emerging Leaders, launched to identify, educate, and develop the future cadre of leaders committed to America’s national security. ISW views interns as an integral component of its team. ISW has worked with interns to draft, edit, and publish their own research under the mentorship of senior analysts. It has also hired many interns onto its staff. Multimedia & Video Production Internship: ISW’s External Relations Team offers a new opportunity to candidates interested in developing ISW’s multimedia products and assisting the production of high-performing video content to accompany ISW’s research products. The intern will hone vid eo production skills, including recording , editing, and publishing videos to social media. They will have the opportunity to learn more about scriptwriting and multimedia strategy . Over the course of a quarter, the intern will work closely with the External Relations Team and research teams to develop new video concepts and conduct thorough multimedia resea rch to support ISW’s products. The intern will have the opportunity to create and edit videos, graphics, and written material , as well as assist in special projects and company initiatives. Interns will also help develop and execute social media campaigns across platforms like X, Bluesky, Threads, LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram . This internship provides a great opportunity to train alongside a small and flexible external relations team in an engaging and fast-paced work environment. This is a full-time (five days per week) in-person or hybrid internship; part-time or remote work will be considered on a case-by-case basis . To apply, please submit a resume, cover letter, and several examples of produced multimedia content, including videos, graphics, and a writing sample. Qualifications Candidates must be motivated and organized college students or recent graduates with demonstrated proficiency in a related field . Candidates must possess excellent writing, editing, and oral communication skills . Candidates must be proficient in Adobe Suite, including Premiere Pro and/or other video software. Candidates should exhibit an understanding of photo and video equipment and maintenance. Candidates should have an eye for visual storytelling, pacing, and brand consistency . Demonstrate an above-average knowledge of social media platforms YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, X, and LinkedIn . The candidate will preferably have a demonstrated interest or expertise in national security issues, particularly Russia, Ukraine, China, or issues in the Middle East . The candidate must show commitment to — and interest in — the core mission and values of ISW. Spring 2027 Internship Program Dates: ISW internships start on January 12, 2027. The program will run until May 14. Interns must both be authorized to work in the United States and be physically present in the United States during their internship tenure. Working remotely outside of the United States is not authorized. If you attend a US university on a student visa, you must be eligible for and obtain a CPT authorization before beginning at ISW . Applications will be considered on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Instructions: Please upload your resume, cover letter, and writing/editing sample. If submitting an editing sample, make sure the sample demonstrates the effect of your edits in some manner. Embedded tracked changes work for this purpose as do screenshots of your communications with the writer. You may include full-page screen captures or scans of edited content, but make sure the resolution is high enough for the image to be readable. You may also include a short synopsis explaining how your edits improved the document. Your cover letter and work sample should be no longer than five pages combined; the work sample can be excerpted from a longer paper. ISW will work with students to gain academic credit for internships where applicable. ISW Scholarship Application The Institute for the Study of War will offer intern candidates up to a $1,000 monthly living stipend as part of a scholarship program.* To be considered for the scholarship, candidates must upload a scholarship application as part of their internship application. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Candidates will be assessed based on the following criteria: Ability to contribute as a member of one of ISW’s research, operations, business development, or external relations teams; and Financial need, such that an unpaid internship would not be possible without assistance. To be considered for the scholarship, candidates must upload a scholarship application as part of their internship application. Within the scholarship application, candidates should upload a 2- to 3-page cover letter which answers each of the following questions. (This should be a different cover letter than the one used for the internship application itself.) Which ISW internship is your top choice? Why do you believe you are qualified? What do you believe to be the most pressing national security problem the US faces today? What solution(s) would you propose? Where do you see yourself in your future career? How will an ISW internship help you get there? Why have you chosen to apply for this supplemental scholarship? Are you currently receiving federal financial aid and/or need-based aid from your university? Feel free to describe using as much detail as you are comfortable. *Please note that the up to $1,000 monthly scholarship is classified as taxable income.

Coordinate user access permissions across core business applications, enforcing established security, password and access standards. IT Operations & Vendor Coordination Partner closely with external IT providers, consultants, and technology vendors to escalate and resolve complex network or technical infrastructure issues. Assist with IT projects, system implementations, technology rollouts, and hardware upgrades as needed Stay current on new tools and technology, and proactively identify opportunities to improve the employee technology experience and streamline or automate repetitive administrative workflows. Requirements: Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science or related field. 1-3 years of experience in IT support, help desk, technical support, or a related role; internship or other relevant hands-on experience will also be considered. Strong proficiency with Apple/macOS and Windows operating systems. Familiarity with cloud-based productivity suites (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Zoom) and common workplace applications. Strong understanding of office networking, Wi-Fi configuration, VPNs, and device management. Exceptional customer service orientation with the ability to communicate technical information clearly and empathetically to non-technical users. Highly organized with rigorous attention to detail and strong follow-through. Strong interest in technology with an eagerness to learn and develop across a broad range of IT functions. Strong problem-solving skills with the self-motivation to troubleshoot common hardware, software, connectivity, and user-access issues independently and know when to escalate. Comfortable working in a fast-paced, growing environment where priorities may shift quickly. Ability to work a flexible part-time schedule on-site at our NYC headquarters as required. The base pay for this position will range from $25-$35/hour. Exact compensation may vary based on job related skills, experience, and location.

## WHAT MAKES US EPIC? At the core of Epic’s success are talented, passionate people. Epic prides itself on creating a collaborative, welcoming, and creative environment. Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating. Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. ### Introduction We value candidates who have significant experience with managing complexity, working independently, and are motivated by hard problems. ### **What We Offer** - The ability to have real impact on mission-critical workflows - The chance to use state-of-the-art tech to solve novel problems with mission partners - The opportunity to define your role through time as we grow - Competitive salary and equity upside with annual merit refreshes based on impact **Position Overview** As a Software Engineer Intern, you’ll work alongside our engineering team to build ConductorAI’s core application: a user-facing web platform for large-scale document search, review, and AI-powered workflows. ## Company Overview Lydian is developing the lowest cost sustainable fuels from waste CO2, water, and renewable electricity to decarbonize the aviation industry. Our breakthrough technology replaces oil and gas refining with fully electrified, modular, and flexible reactor systems that produce fuel with 95% lower emissions than traditional jet fuel. Since our founding in 2021, Lydian has achieved key milestones in record time, including the production of our first liquid fuel from our pilot system, capable of producing 10,000 gallons of fuel per year for a fraction of the capital and time of alternative approaches. We are building a motivated, diverse, and collaborative team that is passionate about addressing the growing climate crisis and is committed to excellence in their work. In particular, we look for tenacious people who are energized by solving the hardest, highest impact problems that come their way. ## Position Overview Lydian is looking for a 6-month Chemical Synthesis Engineer/Scientist Co-op for Spring 2026 to design, synthesize, and test novel catalyst materials for our high-temperature reactor systems, including wet-chemical synthesis of new formulations, bench-scale reactor testing under realistic operating conditions, and characterization of material performance and degradation. In this role, you will prepare and test catalyst formulations designed to operate under demanding high-temperature reactor conditions, and help carry the most promising candidates from bench-scale synthesis through to larger substrates. You will interface with engineers and scientists across various domains in order to inform your experimental design and research priorities, and your results will directly shape which materials advance toward our pilot and commercial systems. This is an hourly position based in Boston, MA and has a minimum commitment of 6-months. The role is fully in-person and hands-on in the lab. ## Responsibilities - Synthesis of novel catalyst formulations to meet demanding reactor requirements (operation for 1000+ h at 1000+ °C), including preparation of supports, active phases, and precursor solutions - Reactor testing to efficiently identify the most promising formulations for further development, including loading and operating bench-scale test reactors and tracking activity, selectivity, and stability over time - Scale-up of promising formulations to coat large substrates (catalyst monoliths > 5 in long), adapting bench-scale recipes to larger batch sizes and coating processes - Working effectively with partners, including automotive catalyst suppliers, to develop scalable manufacturing techniques and transfer Lydian formulations to partner processes - Using advanced characterization techniques (e.g., surface area and porosity, XRD, electron microscopy, chemisorption, thermal analysis) to develop understanding of materials and degradation mechanisms, and working with external partners who can perform some techniques under our guidance - Collaborating with the other projects to understand and incorporate requirements and cooperatively solve problems, particularly around reactor design, coatings, and system integration - Own, develop, and execute synthesis plans of candidate catalyst materials with guidance from Lydian engineers, including defining hypotheses, selecting variables, and prioritizing experiments - Perform analysis of experimental data, prepare reports, and maintain database of catalyst formulations and experimental performance so that results are traceable and can inform future development ## Qualifications - B.S. or M.S. candidate in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or related field. - Hands-on experience with chemical synthesis and general wet lab techniques (e.g., solution preparation, impregnation or precipitation methods, drying and calcination, handling of powders and solvents). - Understanding of reaction kinetics, heat transfer, and mass transport at an undergraduate level; familiarity with heterogeneous catalysis concepts is a plus. - Ability to plan, document, and execute experiments; collect and analyze data; and apply statistical analysis - Strong focus on safe lab practices with foresight to identify and mitigate potential hazards, including safe handling of chemicals, high-temperature furnaces, and compressed gases. - Curiosity, eagerness to learn, and a proactive mindset; comfortable asking questions and taking initiative in an environment where procedures are still being developed. - Strong written and verbal communication skills for sharing results with a cross-functional team. - Desire to work in a fast-paced environment and solve interesting technical problems. ## **Company culture and benefits** - Paid lab/engineering-focused internship with a collaborative in-person technical team - Challenging, meaningful work that can directly impact company success - Opportunities for networking/exposure within the climate tech community - Mentorship from a great team of engineers and scientists
