description: **About Us** SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. **Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja**, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world. **AI at SharkNinja** At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in. **Join the SharkNinja Early Edge Experience:** Built for early career talent. Geared toward impact. Driven by speed. Whether you’re in a co-op or internship, our early talent program is designed to provide valuable exposure to the industry and a fast-paced professional environment. You’ll dive into meaningful projects and tasks that sharpen your skills and deepen your knowledge. Along the way, you’ll benefit from professional development opportunities, community events, and connections that make your experience well-rounded and enriching. Your time with us will culminate in an opportunity to showcase your contributions and learnings to SharkNinja leaders because this is a program for those ready to shape what’s next — fast. Are you the person who takes the product apart to see how it works, then redesigns it in your head? Do you want to know why people buy what they buy — and then go build the thing they didn’t know they needed? Are you excited by the challenge of turning an insight into a product that lands in millions of homes? If so, we invite you to learn more about Product Development, Design & Consumer Insights Co-op opportunities at SharkNinja. This is a single application for product development, design, and consumer insights early talent roles across SharkNinja. The hiring teams are spread across our product development, industrial and experience design, culinary, consumer insights, and consumer experience functions. Whichever team you join, you’ll work on real products and real launches alongside people who have shipped them before. You might be sketching a concept that becomes a hero product, specifying the exact color and finish a consumer sees on the shelf, running usability sessions on a connected app, testing recipes to prove out what an appliance can really do, digging into field feedback to close a consumer pain point, or synthesizing research into the recommendation that changes a product’s direction. If you’re curious, consumer-obsessed, hands-on, and ready to make an impact from day one, we want to hear from you! **Teams that you can be connected to through this posting include:** - Product Development (Shark, Ninja, and Beauty) - Ninja Test Kitchen / Culinary Development - Industrial Design - CMF (Color, Material & Finish) Design - UX/UI Design - Consumer Insights - Customer Experience & Product Support **Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do:** - Contribute to real product launches across Shark, Ninja, and Beauty, from early research and concepting through to shelf - Translate consumer insights into product and design decisions that shape what actually gets built - Bring ideas to life through sketches, renderings, prototypes, wireframes, and design specifications - Conduct hands-on product testing and competitive research, and document findings that influence design direction - Present your work and the thinking behind it to cross-functional partners and design leads — and incorporate their feedback - Collaborate across Product Development, Industrial Design, Engineering, Marketing, Consumer Insights, and Product Management - Gain exposure to the full product development cycle, solving simultaneously for performance, cost, and delight - Own a meaningful project end to end and present your contributions to SharkNinja leaders Depending on the team, your day-to-day may include: **Product Development, Insights & Consumer Experience** - Developing user-relevant design targets for product performance and user experience — human factors, touchpoints, KPIs, and Consumer Satisfaction Indicators — and championing them to engineers, industrial designers, and commercial marketers - Acting as a product “expert” for cross-functional questions, and assisting with new product setups, product information management, and competitive landscape development - Supporting qualitative and quantitative research, designing and refining research tools such as surveys and discussion guides, and translating unmet and latent needs into clear recommendations for new products and features - Building customer personas and journey maps, identifying whitespace opportunities and consumer pain points, and monitoring competitors and market trends to inform positioning - Supporting the post-purchase consumer journey — replacement component specifications, self-service content, and consumer-facing artwork assets - Culinary testing and hero recipe development alongside food scientists and research chefs, evaluating performance and quality for launches such as the Ninja Creami, Crispi, and Luxe Café - Recording test results accurately and synthesizing insights into stories that influence brand, product, and executive strategy **Industrial, CMF & Digital Experience Design** - Translating consumer insights into bold, user-centered design solutions through sketches, illustrations, and high-fidelity renderings - Creating product designs in SolidWorks or Rhino, producing renderings in KeyShot, and collaborating with Engineering to deliver clean, production-ready CAD files - Specifying the full look and feel of a product — surface finish, color, material, texture, and branding — and creating, tracking, and maintaining color specifications (ID SPECS) - Developing color palette proposals targeted for different retailers, organizing supplier CMF samples into a material library, and working to standards such as Pantone, NCS, SPI, YickSang, and Mold-Tech - Supporting UI design, icon design, and rating/warning label creation, and interacting daily with the APAC manufacturing team, suppliers, and the Compliance team - Creating wireframes, interactive prototypes, and visual design specs in Figma, Adobe XD, or Sketch for mobile app and embedded UI experiences - Participating in usability testing, maintaining and evolving design systems for cross-platform consistency, and designing for accessibility, responsiveness, and internationalization - Building visual and functional prototypes, and exploring emerging trends, new materials, and future-forward aesthetics **ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS:** - Current student in a related bachelor's or master’s or PhD program or has graduated from such a program within the past year — Industrial Design, Product Design, UX/UI or Interaction Design, Mechanical Engineering, Marketing, Market Research, Psychology or Sociology, Culinary Arts or Food Science, Business, Communications, or similar - Must be able to work a full-time, 40-hour-per-week onsite-hybrid schedule; specific location and number of onsite days vary by team and term - A consumer-first perspective and real curiosity about how people actually use products in their homes - Strong visual and verbal storytelling — you can present an idea, explain the thinking behind it, and take feedback well - Meticulous attention to detail, and the discipline to hold onto it under tight deadlines - Strong organizational and project management instincts; comfortable juggling multiple projects and shifting priorities - Hands-on and resourceful — willing to build the rough version, test it, and iterate - Able to synthesize complex or messy input into clear, actionable recommendations - Collaborative and positive in brainstorms, critiques, and reviews - Proficient in Microsoft 365, particularly PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook - Prior internship, co-op, studio, kitchen, research, or personal project experience is a strong asset **Any of the following are a plus — we don’t expect all of them:** - CAD and 3D: SolidWorks, Creo, or Rhino; rendering in KeyShot - Adobe Creative Suite: Illustrator, InDesign, and Photoshop - Design and prototyping tools: Figma, Adobe XD, or Sketch - Prototyping and shop competency: 3D printing, machine shop equipment, building in plastic and metal - Color and materials standards: Pantone, NCS, SPI, YickSang, Mold-Tech; interest in color communication toward international standards - Basic understanding of electronics commonly used in small appliances (motors, sensors, PCBAs) - Accessibility best practices and responsive design principles; interest in connected consumer products, smart home technology, or IoT ecosystems - Coursework in market research, consumer insights, psychology, sociology, or related social sciences - Prior experience in food service, recipe testing, or culinary R&D - Project tracking and file management tools such as Asana, Monday, Airtable, Box, or SharePoint **Work samples:** If you’re interested in a design role — Industrial Design, CMF, or UX/UI — please include a portfolio that demonstrates your design process, not just your finished work. You can link it in your resume or attach it in the cover letter field. A portfolio is not required for consideration for Product Development, Ninja Test Kitchen, Consumer Insights, or Customer Experience & Product Support. ***This evergreen job post is for upcoming Product Development, Design & Consumer Insights Co-ops at SharkNinja. We’re continuously seeking exceptional candidates who aspire to make a positive impact on people’s lives. Your application will be thoroughly reviewed for potential future opportunities within our team. We encourage you to explore all relevant current openings and apply accordingly.*** **Salary and Other Compensation:** The hourly salary range for this position is displayed below. Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience and other qualifications of the successful candidate. The Company offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements: medical insurance, health savings account (HSA) with company contribution, sick time, company holidays, employee product discount, product testing opportunities, referral bonuses, and more. Hourly Pay Range $26—$35 USD **Our Culture** At SharkNinja, we don’t just raise the bar—we push past it every single day. **Our Outrageously Extraordinary mindset** drives us to tackle the impossible, push boundaries, and deliver results that others only dream of. If you thrive on breaking out of your swim lane, you’ll be right at home. **What We Offer** We offer competitive health insurance, retirement plans, paid time off, employee stock purchase options, wellness programs, SharkNinja product discounts, and more. **We empower your personal and professional growth** with high impact Learning Programs featuring bold voices redefining what’s possible. **When you join, you’re not just part of a company—you’re part of an outrageously extraordinary community.** Together, we won’t just launch products—**we’ll disrupt entire markets.** At SharkNinja, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion are vital to our global success. Valuing each unique voice and blending all of our diverse skills strengthens SharkNinja’s innovation every day. We support ALL associates in bringing their authentic selves to work, making an impact, and having the opportunity for career acceleration. With help from our leadership, associates, and our community, we aim to have equity be a key component of the SharkNinja DNA. Learn more about us: [Life At SharkNinja](https://www.instagram.com/sharkninja/) [**Outrageously Extraordinary**](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLmRfBxyGu_mKl9SF12lM1NAIx-z07uLNQ) **SharkNinja Candidate Privacy Notice** - For candidates based in **all regions**, please refer to this [Candidate Privacy Notice](https://www.sharkninja.com/candidate-privacy-notice.html). - For candidates based in **China**, please refer to this [Candidate Privacy Notice](https://www.sharkninja.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice-china.html). - For candidates based in **Vietnam**, please refer to this [Candidate Privacy Notice](https://www.sharkninja.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice-vietnam.html). *We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other class protected by legislation, and local law. SharkNinja will consider reasonable accommodations consistent with legislation, and local law. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact SharkNinja People & Culture at [accommodations@sharkninja.com](mailto:accommodations@sharkninja.com)*

Whichever team you join, you’ll work on real products and real launches alongside people who have shipped them before. You might be sketching a concept that becomes a hero product, specifying the exact color and finish a consumer sees on the shelf, running usability sessions on a connected app, testing recipes to prove out what an appliance can really do, digging into field feedback to close a consumer pain point, or synthesizing research into the recommendation that changes a product’s direction. Strong visual and verbal storytelling — you can present an idea, explain the thinking behind it, and take feedback well - Meticulous attention to detail, and the discipline to hold onto it under tight deadlines - Strong organizational and project management instincts; comfortable juggling multiple projects and shifting priorities - Hands-on and resourceful — willing to build the rough version, test it, and iterate - role: 2027 Applied Science Internship - Automated Reasoning - United States, PhD Student Science Recruiting, Automated Reasoning
description: This role sits within Amazon's Automated Reasoning and Formal Verification research horizon. Shape the Future of Cloud Computing. Are you a graduate student passionate about Automated Reasoning and its real-world applications? Join our team of innovators and embark on a journey to revolutionize cloud computing through innovative automated reasoning techniques. Our tools are called billions of times daily, powering the backbone of Amazon's products and services. We are changing the way computer systems are developed and operated, raising the bar for security, durability, availability, and quality. Applied Scientists in Automated Reasoning develop and apply formal methods, automated reasoning techniques, and neurosymbolic approaches to ensure the security, reliability, and correctness of Amazon and AWS services and customer applications. Application areas span cloud infrastructure verification, cryptographic assurance, AI safety, and formal guarantees for generative AI systems. Methods range from interactive theorem proving and constraint solving to neuro-inspired proof search. As an Applied Science Intern, you will have the opportunity to work alongside our scientists and contribute to projects. From distributed proof search and SAT/SMT solvers to program analysis, synthesis, and verification, you will tackle complex challenges at the intersection of theory and practice. # ABOUT CYVL The best infrastructure is invisible. You only notice it when it fails. For decades, the people responsible for our roads, bridges and sidewalks have been asked to manage the physical world with tools that can't see it. Cyvl is the Physical AI company changing that. We build purpose-built sensors, computer vision and AI that turn every drive into current data: what exists, where it is and what condition it's in. 500+ cities and towns use our Infrastructure Intelligence Platform to direct the work and fix problems before they fail. 1 in 30 Americans drive on roads managed with Cyvl data. The proof isn't a dashboard. It's a smoother commute, a safer walk to school and public dollars going where they matter most. We're a fast-moving team in Boston building hardware, software and AI for the real world. If you believe technology's highest calling is public good, come build with us. # THE ROLE You'll join the Data Operations team, the group that turns raw street-level capture into the map layers 500+ cities rely on. Every day, sensor data from the field flows through our processing pipelines and comes out as road conditions, sidewalk inventories, sign catalogs, and pavement scores. You'll own pieces of that pipeline: running deliveries end to end, catching data problems before a customer does, and writing the scripts that make the next delivery faster than the last. ## WHAT YOU'LL DO - Process customer deliveries end to end: run geospatial data through our Python pipelines, validate the output, and publish the final layers to the Cyvl platform. - Build QC checks that review data automatically. - Investigate failed and stalled processing jobs in our AWS pipelines, find the root cause, and document the fix. - Automate recurring manual steps into repeatable scripts and runbooks, and measure the time saved. - Partner with engineering and customer success to turn field-reported issues into code fixes or process improvements. ## WHAT YOU BRING - Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field - Proficiency in Python; comfortable writing scripts that read, transform, and validate data - Comfort working in a terminal and with version control - Available full-time for 10-12 weeks in Summer 2027, based in our Somerville office ## NICE TO HAVE - GIS experience (QGIS or ArcGIS, and formats like GeoJSON, shapefiles, GeoPackage) - Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, especially AWS - SQL and experience querying real datasets - Exposure to geospatial Python libraries (geopandas, shapely) - Interest in civic infrastructure, transportation, or public-sector technology - A knack for the business side: you think about how data drives decisions and like problems like "how do we track this better" or "how do we make this visible to the team" - Experience building dashboards or turning data into something a non-technical person can act on # WHY CYVL **Hard tech. Real streets. Your name on it.** - **Hard problems in the real world.** You build end-to-end: our own hardware, software and AI, with work that shows up on the street in the real world. - **Ownership that compounds.** You own outcomes, not tasks. You work directly with customers and across our team, and you'll own more, sooner, than almost anywhere else. - **Intense, with heart.** We're building a category, so it's not a place to coast. We also take care of each other, have genuine fun together, and believe in what we are doing. ## WHAT WE ASK - **Cross lanes.** "Not my job" doesn't exist here. - **Own without a playbook.** The plan is still being written, often by you. - **Try, miss, try again.** We make big bets. Some won't land, and we learn fast. - **Be in the room.** We're on-site in Somerville about 90% of the time. We're a startup building a category. If that sounds like the draw, not the risk, we'd love to talk. ## OUR VALUES - **Real:** Authentic and transparent. Focused on solving real problems with simple, effective solutions. - **All Out:** Bold, driven, and committed to delivering results that matter. - **Accelerating:** Always learning, growing, and moving with intention. - **Reliable:** We follow through and deliver at a consistently high bar. - **Empowering:** We lift each other up and help governments build infrastructure they can be proud of. ## SEE OUR WORK - [How Atlanta cut downtown potholes by 60%](https://cyvl.com/case-studies/atlanta-ga) - [How Buffalo turned a campaign promise into a paving plan](https://cyvl.com/case-studies/buffalo-ny) - [How to rebuild US infrastructure smarter](https://www.theengineer.co.uk/content/opinion/how-to-rebuild-us-infrastructure-smarter-and-stronger) ## WANT TO GO THE EXTRA MILE? (OPTIONAL) If you're excited about this role and want to tell us more, email with the subject line "Data Ops Intern, [Your Name]" and answer any or all of these: 1. Why Cyvl, and why a startup? What draws you to this kind of work, and to a small team where your work ships right away? 2. What's the coolest thing you've built with AI? A class project, side project, script, or experiment all count. Tell us what it did and what you learned. 3. Tell us about a time you solved a problem by fixing the process instead of just working harder. What was slowing you down? What did you change? What happened? A few honest paragraphs beat an AI-slop essay. Links to code, notebooks, or demos are welcome. **We build for every community, so we hire from all of them.** The best people for this work come from different backgrounds, paths, and places, and many of them don't check every box. If this role excites you, apply anyway. If you need an adjustment to our interview process, tell us and we'll make it work.

# **What We Do** Gecko Robotics is helping the world’s most important organizations ensure the availability, reliability, and sustainability of critical infrastructure. This enables real-time decision making to increase the efficiency and safety of operations, promote mission readiness, and protect the environment and civilization from the effects of infrastructure failure. **Role at a Glance** Gecko Robotics is seeking a **Full Stack Software Engineering Intern** to join our Engineering team in New York for **Summer 2027**. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday. Gecko’s Engineering teams build customer-facing applications that turn robot, sensor, and document data into decisions about the health of critical infrastructure. You will work across the stack on a defined project: building frontend workflows, backend services, and data pipelines that make complex asset data usable by the people who maintain it. The specific tools will depend on the assigned project. **About You** You are a builder who likes seeing your work used. You are comfortable moving between frontend and backend, you break large problems into shippable pieces, and you communicate clearly about what you built, what you learned, and what you would do next. **Required Skills** - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related technical discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028. - Ability to work onsite in New York, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship. - Foundational programming experience in Python and JavaScript or TypeScript, including object-oriented or functional programming concepts. - Experience building a web application end to end (frontend and backend) through coursework, projects, research, hackathons, or a prior internship. - Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems. - Understanding of relational databases and REST APIs. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work, explain tradeoffs, and collaborate on ambiguous problems. - Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback. **Preferred Skills** - Experience with React and TypeScript in a real project. - Experience designing data schemas or working with messy, real-world datasets. - Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP, and to containers such as Docker. - Exposure to integrating LLM or other AI APIs into an application. - Interest in 3D, visualization, or spatial data. - Interest in industrial, defense, or infrastructure applications where reliability matters. # **Who We Are** At Gecko, our people are our greatest investment. Ultimately, we care about the outcomes we achieve - and creating a culture of autonomy and trust that enables that impact. Our smart, rugged radios and connected cloud ecosystem harness the power of voice and AI to close this digital chasm. We’re building tools that meet frontline workers where they are, capturing tribal knowledge, and turning communication into action. By transforming every spoken word into intelligence, we’re delivering safety, productivity, and empowerment to the workers who keep our world moving. We are looking for a Software Engineer Intern who is a motivated and ambitious undergraduate (or graduate) student with an expected graduation date of December 2027 or Spring 2028 to join our mobile device product team. This opportunity is a **paid internship during the summer 2027**. High-performing interns may be considered for full-time roles after graduation, depending on business needs. **What makes our Sumer Intern program different:** - Executive and senior leadership team exposure - regular touchpoints with Relay's leadership team, including Q&A coffee chats, Breakfast with the CEO, and working sessions. - Cross-functional cohort - work alongside interns across every part of the business, not just your team. - Structured learning - regular skill-building sessions covering topics from product strategy to financial modeling to sales craft to professional networking and interviewing skills. - Real ownership - you'll own a project from kickoff to final presentation, with mentors and fellow Relayers who are invested in your success. - Intern showcase - present your work to the full company at the end of the summer - Raleigh HQ experience - team lunches, volunteer Intern Impact day, social events, and a chance to see how a scaling tech company operates up close! Interns will gain hands-on experience across the full device stack, from Android application development and OS-level systems programming to embedded firmware and Linux hardware interfaces — contributing to a product that ships to real customers every 6 weeks. We work with a diverse set of languages, including C, C++, Java, Kotlin, Rust, and Bash/Python. Our devices run Android on custom in-house hardware, and our development environments are Linux-based. **About Us** At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. **About the Summer Internship Program** Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: **Cohort #1** Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 **Cohort #2** Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at our Torrance headquarters and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package. **About the Role** As a Software Intern, you will work on the infrastructure and tooling that enables Antares teams to deploy, monitor, and operate internal applications and compute workloads. You will own substantive projects spanning cloud deployment tooling, systems automation, observability, data project infrastructure, and cluster operations. You will work across both cloud and on-premises infrastructure, improving how applications and data projects are deployed and monitored while helping make internal compute resources more reliable, recoverable, and efficient. This role is well suited for someone who enjoys building practical tools, automating manual processes, and improving the systems other technical teams rely on. **Roles and Responsibilities:** - Improve cloud deployment tooling for shared internal applications - Automate integrations between internal and external systems - Create Grafana dashboards and alerts to improve visibility into internal systems - Build standardized templates for Python data projects that improve deployment, monitoring, and dependency management - Document quality processes so they can be consistently used by non-software developers - Migrate cluster infrastructure to the latest versions of Rocky Linux and Warewulf - Build storage tooling to improve recovery and performance - Analyze and optimize cloud costs for internal job pipelines - Create dashboards that provide visibility into cluster usage - Build tooling to help teams better understand and optimize their use of shared compute resources **Basic Qualifications:** - Enrolled in at least a bachelor’s degree program, and going into your Junior or Senior year of studies - Must have prior internship experience, or significant (>1yr) project team, laboratory, or research experience **Preferred Skills & Experience:** - GPA of 3.5 or above - Experience in a University club or organization, leadership role preferred - Strong interpersonal and technical communication skills (examples: leading a student project team, presenting research at conferences, etc.) - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail - Ability to work cross-departmentally with different groups and teams - Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements - Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively **Location** - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises. **Culture** At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - *Think in Systems* - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - *Obsess over the End User* - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - *Be Unconstrained by Convention* - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - *Go Where the Work I*s - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - *Operate in the Grey* - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. ### **About the Ground Systems Deployment Team** The Ground Systems Deployment and Construction team is responsible for turning bare ground into functional drone charging sites! We’re a broad, cross-functional team with skills across civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, and construction engineering with a mandate to deliver world-class construction execution with zero issues in the first 30 days, on-time and on-budget, using scalable, cost-optimized, and serviceable designs. ### **The Role** The Ground System Deployment and Construction Engineering team is seeking a curious, collaborative Electrical Engineering Intern to support the design and deployment of Zipline’s Ground Systems across a variety of sites and applications. In this role, you’ll gain hands-on experience with commercial and light-industrial electrical distribution as applied to an autonomous drone delivery network. Working alongside experienced engineers, you’ll help with utility coordination, site-level electrical design, structure-level wiring approaches, and technical documentation. You’ll collaborate with mechanical, structural, electrical, and deployments teams to support real-world projects and contribute to problem-solving as new challenges arise. This internship also offers opportunities to explore new design ideas and assist with improvements to our engineering processes. You’ll work and become familiar with the National Electrical Code and apply the concepts to site and infrastructure designs. The internship is based in South San Francisco, with occasional travel within California and the U.S. for site visits or field support. ### **What You'll Do** - Support engineers with research, drafting, and documentation for electrical distribution and structure-level wiring designs aligned with NEC and relevant standards. - Assist with UL/TUV certification efforts by gathering documentation, preparing technical materials, and coordinating with engineering partners. - Help prepare materials, track communication, and support interactions with deployment and construction teams - Implement feedback from Deployment and Construction teams to continuously optimize designs for more efficient build and scale - Design electrical distribution of commercial and light industrial ground system projects per NEC and relevant applicable codes and standards. - Design next generation charging structure level electrical wiring and installation approaches. - Evaluate all options and a lean budget, select best vendors to ensure reliable and quality services and products. - Help document project risks, prepare materials for meetings, support communication across teams, and occasionally participate in site visits for field observations. - Create documentation to ensure quality and process refinement between each build to help with consistent scale - Collaborate with engineering and business teams to understand customer needs and contribute to improvements in Ground Systems infrastructure. - Travel to commercial and flight test sites may be required on an ad hoc basis. ### **What You'll Bring** - You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies, with relevant coursework (e.g., circuits, power systems, construction). Master's and PhD students are also eligible. - Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and a willingness to ask questions and learn. - Familiarity with engineering tools or concepts such as CAD/ECAD, electrical modeling, or basic simulation software. (Revit, Bluebeam Revu, AutoCAD, NX) - Clear written and verbal communication skills, especially when summarizing technical information. - Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment and support a wide range of tasks. - Curiosity, initiative, and a proactive approach to problem-solving. Comfort with hands-on work and openness to occasional travel (if needed). - An open mind to help us bring Zipline’s service to new and existing customers! ### **What Else You Should Know** *This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September).* The hourly rate for this internship is $44 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. ### **Voluntary Self-Identification** For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

**Overview** Inferact's mission is to grow vLLM as the world's AI inference engine and accelerate AI progress by making inference cheaper and faster. Founded by the creators and core maintainers of vLLM, we sit at the intersection of models and hardware, a position that took years to build. **About the Role** We're looking for exceptional University of Waterloo co-op students who want to work on the systems that determine how fast, efficiently, and reliably frontier AI models run on frontier workloads at scale. This is not a sandboxed internship project. We will match your strengths and interests to a real engineering problem across the vLLM stack, from model execution and low-level accelerator code to distributed serving and the cloud platform that makes it all usable. You'll work alongside the creators and core maintainers of vLLM on work intended to ship into open source, production systems, or the tooling that supports both. You will have a primary technical track, meaningful ownership, and mentorship from a small, senior team, with opportunities to collaborate across models, compilers, accelerators, networking, and distributed systems. The goal is to let exceptional students learn at the frontier while making contributions used by developers and AI teams around the world. **Potential Focus Areas** Your co-op will have a primary home in one of the following tracks, with opportunities to contribute across others: - **Inference Runtime:** Bring new model architectures and inference techniques to life in vLLM. Implement ideas from research papers; support mixture-of-experts, multimodal, diffusion, and agentic workloads; and improve scheduling, continuous batching, KV-cache memory management, prefix caching, and hybrid model serving. - **Performance & Scale:** Build the distributed serving data plane that lets vLLM run across many GPUs and nodes. Work on tensor, expert, or context parallelism; prefill/decode separation and KV-cache transport; fault tolerance and multi-tenancy; and high-performance communication using NCCL, DeepEP, NVSHMEM, RDMA, or InfiniBand. - **Kernel Engineering:** Raise the hardware performance ceiling by writing and optimizing attention, GEMM, sampling, KV-cache, fused, and quantization kernels. Use CUDA, Triton, TileLang, CUTLASS/CUTE, or related tools; reason about memory hierarchy, occupancy, and tensor cores; and prove speedups through profiling, correctness tests, and reproducible benchmarks. - **AMD GPU Performance:** Help make vLLM first-class on AMD accelerators. Work across ROCm, HIP, Triton, CK, AITER, kernels, runtime paths, quantization, compiler integration, and performance-regression infrastructure while learning how AMD-specific execution, memory, and toolchain constraints shape inference. - **TPU Performance:** Help make vLLM fast and correct on Google TPUs. Build backend, runtime, and compiler integrations with JAX, XLA, Pallas, MLIR, and related tooling; inspect compiler artifacts; work on lowering, fusion, and code generation; and benchmark production-relevant serving across correctness, latency, and throughput. - **Cloud Orchestration:** Build the operational platform that makes large-scale inference deployable and reliable. Work on Kubernetes and custom operators, topology-aware GPU scheduling, zero-downtime vLLM rollouts, token-aware routing, observability, infrastructure-as-code, automated recovery, and bring-your-own-cloud or multi-cloud fleet management. You are not expected to arrive with experience in every track. We care most about unusual depth or learning velocity in one area, strong fundamentals, and evidence that you can turn a difficult problem into working, measurable software. **Skills and Qualifications** Minimum qualifications: - Currently pursuing a bachelor's, master's, or PhD degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, or a related technical field, and eligible for a University of Waterloo co-op work term. - Strong programming ability in Python, C++, Rust, Go, or another systems-oriented language. - Strong computer science fundamentals and the ability to learn from research papers, technical documentation, and complex systems code. - Evidence that you have built and debugged nontrivial software through coursework, research, a prior internship, open-source work, or an ambitious side project. - A builder mindset: you define what success means, measure results, validate correctness, communicate clearly, and keep iterating until the system works. Preferred qualifications: - Depth in at least one relevant area such as ML or inference systems, distributed systems, GPU or accelerator programming, compilers, high-performance computing, operating systems, networking, Kubernetes, or cloud infrastructure. - Hands-on experience with one or more relevant technologies such as PyTorch, vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, CUDA, Triton, TileLang, ROCm/HIP, JAX/XLA, Pallas, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Ray, or SLURM. - Experience profiling or benchmarking software, validating numerical or systems correctness, or building tests that protect against performance regressions. - Experience with systems beyond a single local process or device, including multi-GPU, multi-node, research-cluster, high-throughput, or production-like workloads. Bonus points if you have: - Contributed to open-source ML, systems, compiler, or infrastructure projects, especially vLLM or adjacent projects. - Built a research system, benchmark suite, compiler or kernel project, distributed service, or infrastructure tool that demonstrates unusual technical depth and initiative. - Worked across more than one layer of the stack and enjoy moving between algorithms, runtimes, systems, and hardware rather than staying inside a single abstraction. - Created a technical artifact such as a paper, design document, blog post, demo, or talk that clearly explains what you built and what you learned. **Meet Inferact at Waterloo** Interested in learning more about Inferact, vLLM, and the engineering problems you could work on during your co-op? Join us for our **University of Waterloo Employer Information Session** to meet the team, learn more about Inferact, and hear about the Inference Engineering Co-op opportunity. - **Venue:** Tatham Centre, Room 2218 - **Date:** Monday, October 5, 2026 - **Time:** 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM ET **Logistics** - **Location:** San Francisco, California. This co-op is in-office only at Inferact's San Francisco office and is intended for the University of Waterloo co-op program. - **Work term:** Co-op / internship. Exact dates will align with the applicable Waterloo work term. - **Compensation:** Competitive compensation based on the applicable co-op market and candidate background, plus a housing stipend for the duration of the co-op term.

### **A Foundational Company** Rilla is on a mission to index the offline world. Today, we’ve built the leading sales coaching software for organizations doing sales offline. We have over 1000 customers, including The Home Depot, KKR, Neighborly, and PulteGroup, using our product to enable AI sales coaching across their organization. We are backed by Google Ventures, Bessemer Ventures, Crew Capital, and Broom Ventures, along with others. We’re an in office team in NYC with builders who operate like high speed reinforcement learners. We obsess over our customers, move at a high velocity, are not afraid of failure, and look to maximize our real-world impact. If you want to build the products and systems for how billions of conversations in the real world are captured and indexed, Rilla is the place to do it. ### **The Role** Rilla engineers architect and ship features across the stack at lightning speed. On a daily basis, you will build end-to-end workflows, take them to production, and solve real world problems across an out-sized scale. As an early technical steward, you will raise the bar for code quality and decision‑making, setting patterns that cement a world‑class engineering culture as we scale. While the company 10×’s, your scope and ownership will grow just as fast—building the tools, mental models, and platforms that let both you and Rilla accelerate exponentially. Do you describe yourself as "obsessive"? Do you aspire to be a founder or a leader in applying AI to the physical world? We believe Rilla is the best place — with the best peers — to learn how. ### **Technologies We Use** - Different languages and frameworks, including React, React Native, Typescript and Python - Open-source technologies like Node.js, PostgreSQL, Turborepo, Lodash, and Zod - Industry-standard build tooling, including GitHub Actions, Terraform, and Spacelift ### **What We Value** - An **infinite learner**. Someone who is relentless in their curiosity. - A **customer obsessive**. Someone who deeply care about delighting customers and solving real pains, not vanity metrics. - A **winning attitude**. You thrive with extreme accountability, learning as a team, and both giving and receiving rapid feedback. - **Extreme empathy.** Our customers are not tech companies. They live and work in the real world. Empathy is critical to arriving at correct solutions. - **Unafraid of failure.** You take risks. You see failure as an opportunity to learn, grow, and be better the next time. In a weird way, you trick your brain into being excited when you fail, because it means you got a new opportunity to learn more. ### **What We Require** - Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Javascript, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages. - Strong engineering prowess, ideally developed at start-ups. - Familiarity with storage and data processing systems, cloud infrastructure, and other technical tools. - Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality. ### **Don’t Work Here** Please don't join if you're not excited about: 1. Building an AI product for an industry untouched by modern software 2. Constantly talking to and visiting customers in the field 3. Working ~60 hrs/week in person with some of the most ambitious people in NYC 4. Attempting to build a generational company, and the intensity required to do so Our benefits aim to empower Rilla employees in removing roadblocks to achieving their life’s work. The list below details our available benefits and some of the perks that can be enjoyed as an employee of Rilla. ### **Benefits** - Medical, dental, and vision insurance - Breakfast, lunch, dinner, and supplementary food and drink — 6x a week - Gym membership - Commuter benefits - Relocation assistance - Take what you need paid time off, not accrual based - $1,000 stipend for learning and personal growth - $1,500 a month rent stipend - Tech equipment - Unlimited token budget

description: ## **About Abridge** Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients. Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems. We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh. ## The Role We're looking for early-career Software Engineers who are highly driven and passionate about making a real-world impact through AI for healthcare. You'll join a cross-functional team of researchers, clinicians, and engineers to help translate cutting-edge language model capabilities into dependable clinical systems. You'll be building AI-powered features that touch real clinical workflows, shipping production code, and growing fast in an environment where GenAI is at the center of everything we build. You will be given an unusual amount of responsibility and autonomy. You will be surrounded by people who want to do their best work. You will experience accelerated learning and career growth. You will have a path to become a future leader of the company. The journey will be demanding but rewarding. ## What You'll Do - Contribute to backend and frontend systems across Abridge - Shift projects, tackling a wide variety of challenges as you grow and upskill at a startup operating at scale - Collaborate across ML, infrastructure, product, and clinical teams — and develop a genuine understanding of the users and clinicians we serve - Contribute to evaluation frameworks that measure accuracy, robustness, and clinical reliability — including automated pipelines and human-in-the-loop review - Think with an agent-first approach. Continuously learn and relearn agentic coding. - Fine-tune your judgment on where the human in the loop is critical. - Help prototype with new models, prompting techniques, and open-source orchestration tools (LangChain, LlamaIndex, etc.) - Build and iterate on agentic LLM systems — including retrieval pipelines, structured tool use, and chained LLM workflows — as part of a collaborative engineering team - Contribute to monitoring and observability systems that keep our LLM workflows healthy in production - Learn from senior engineers and bring curiosity and fresh perspective to every problem ## What You'll Bring - A degree in CS or a related field, or equivalent experience (projects, bootcamp, open source — we care about what you can build not where you learned it) - Hands-on GenAI experience — through coursework, personal projects, internships, or hackathons. You've integrated an LLM API, built a RAG pipeline, experimented with agents, or shipped something AI-powered and can speak to what you learned - Familiarity with LLM orchestration concepts (prompt chaining, tool use, retrieval) even if you haven't yet used them in a production setting - AI tooling is already part of how you work — you use it to write, debug, and learn faster, and you know when to trust it vs. verify - Curiosity about model evaluation, failure modes, and what it actually takes to make an LLM system reliable - Collaborative, low-ego mindset — we move fast, and we need teammates who pitch in wherever needed **How we work** We’re a fast-moving team. New grads join us in the office five days a week in [SF/NYC] because we learn fastest, and ship fastest, when we’re side by side. You’ll own real work early. Within your first weeks expect to build and ship out features. The pace is high, and there are stretches (launches, production issues, tight deadlines) when the team stays late to get it done. We care about the outcome, and we support each other through those stretches. **You’ll thrive here if you:** - Take initiative and don’t wait to be told what’s next - Stay with a hard problem when you’re stuck - Care about the outcome, not just finishing the task - Want to learn quickly and are comfortable with high expectations ## **Why Work at Abridge?** At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month. Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business. Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients. We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life. If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you. ## **How we take care of Abridgers:** - **Generous Time Off**: 14 paid holidays, flexible PTO for salaried employees, and accrued time off for hourly employees - **Comprehensive Health Plans**: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for all full-time employees and their families. - **Generous HSA Contribution**: If you choose a High Deductible Health Plan, Abridge makes monthly contributions to your HSA. - **Paid Parental Leave**: Generous paid parental leave for all full-time employees. - **Family Forming Benefits:** Resources and financial support to help you build your family. - **401(k) Matching**: Contribution matching to help invest in your future. - **Personal Device Allowance**: Tax free funds for personal device usage. - **Pre-tax Benefits:** Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Commuter Benefits. - **Lifestyle Wallet**: Monthly contributions for fitness, professional development, coworking, and more. - **Mental Health Support**: Dedicated access to therapy and coaching to help you reach your goals. - **Sabbatical Leave**: Paid Sabbatical Leave after 5 years of employment. - **Compensation and Equity**: Competitive compensation and equity grants for full time employees. - ... and much more! ## **Equal Opportunity Employer** Abridge is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants equally without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability. We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the interview process. Once you submit your application, we'll follow up with details on how to request an accommodation for interviewing, completing any assessments, or otherwise participating in the selection process. ## **Staying safe - Protect yourself from recruitment fraud** We are aware of individuals and entities fraudulently representing themselves as Abridge recruiters and/or hiring managers. Abridge will never ask for financial information or payment, or for personal information such as bank account number or social security number during the job application or interview process. Any emails from the Abridge recruiting team will come from an @[](http://abridge.com) email address. You can learn more about how to protect yourself from these types of fraud by referring to [this article](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/05/scammers-are-hijacking-job-ads-heres-how-spot-fakes). Please exercise caution and cease communications if something feels suspicious about your interactions.

You will be at the forefront of real-time technology that’s revolutionizing how companies run their businesses every day. Consistent with our commitment to diversity & inclusion, we value individuals with the ability to work on diverse teams and with a diverse range of people. Qualifications Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to visit job sites to inspect existing conditions and document potential scope of work Ability to sit and/or stand for prolonged periods of time at a desk working on a computer and viewing a screen Ability to learn and apply established engineering principles to solve problems and/or overcome obstacles using sound judgment, independent decision making, and prolonged focus Why KPFF? SingleStore Software Engineers are at the forefront of real-time technology that’s revolutionizing how companies run their businesses everyday. With release cycles throughout the year, our engineers are accustomed to moving quickly in a rapid production environment. To do this successfully, we work collaboratively and creatively across teams to maximize our opportunity for impact. We also believe it’s important to celebrate our wins together whether it be at a local spot or getting out of the city for some exploring. As a Software Engineer you will be empowered to own your projects end-to-end and be an active contributor throughout the product life cycle. To expedite your growth path, you will partner with engineers who deeply care about your success and will lend their expertise to your professional development. Our engineers are not just technical partners, but are also business partners who are exposed to all areas of the business, working with teams such as product, marketing, and sales. Role and Responsibilities Our Software Engineers work on small, collaborative teams to help drive our company forward. Whether you’re exploring cutting-edge technologies like LLM and vector index, improving the fault tolerance a SingleStore cluster, accelerating the performance of SQL queries with techniques like SIMD and LLVM codeGen, or writing search and costing modules for the query optimizer, our University Graduates are responsible for brand new and existing projects that are deployed into production with each release. Your work will include everything from writing to testing software, and you’ll gain a significant understanding of both the product and the business. Required Skills and Experience - B.S. Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related discipline - Deep understanding of C.S. fundamentals, in particular operating systems, concurrency, multithreading, and server architectures - Strong programming skills with C++ or C - Passionate about building highly reliable software - Firm grasp of algorithms and data structures SingleStore delivers the cloud-native database with the speed and scale to power the world’s data-intensive applications. With a distributed SQL database that introduces simplicity to your data architecture by unifying transactions and analytics, SingleStore empowers digital leaders to deliver exceptional, real-time data experiences to their customers. SingleStore is venture-backed and headquartered in San Francisco with offices in Sunnyvale, Raleigh, Seattle, Boston, London, Lisbon, Bangalore, Dublin and Kyiv. Consistent with our commitment to diversity & inclusion, we value individuals with the ability to work on diverse teams and with a diverse range of people. SingleStore is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company that does not have a signed agreement with the Company. SingleStore values individuals for their unique skills and experiences, and we’re proud to offer roles in a variety of locations across the United States. Salary is based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location, and is just one part of our total compensation and benefits package. Certain roles are also eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases and annual bonuses.

# **What We Do** Gecko Robotics is helping the world’s most important organizations ensure the availability, reliability, and sustainability of critical infrastructure. Gecko's complete and connected solutions combine wall-climbing robots, industry-leading sensors, and an AI-powered data platform to provide customers with a unique window into the current and future health of their physical assets. This enables real-time decision making to increase the efficiency and safety of operations, promote mission readiness, and protect the environment and civilization from the effects of infrastructure failure. **Role at a Glance** Gecko Robotics is seeking an **Embedded Software Engineering Intern** to join RoboSPLAT within Field Infra in Pittsburgh for **Summer 2027**. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday. RoboSPLAT builds software and tools that help teams develop, deploy, debug, and operate Gecko’s robotic and ultrasonic testing (UT) collection systems. You will work primarily in C/C++ and Python on a defined project that improves system integration, diagnostics, testing, or development workflows. **What you will do** - Develop C/C++ and Python software for a defined embedded software project under the guidance of experienced engineers. - Build or improve tooling, diagnostics, tests, or workflows that reduce friction in developing, debugging, and deploying software on robot hardware. - Work across software and system boundaries by integrating services or hardware-facing interfaces, investigating system behavior, testing solutions, and documenting findings. - Use version control, code review, and structured debugging practices to produce maintainable code. - Collaborate with RoboSPLAT and partner teams, communicate status and tradeoffs clearly, and deliver a final demonstration and handoff. **Technologies We Use (If Applicable)** C/C++, Python, Git, Linux, networking, and ROS 2. Depending on the project, you may also work with the Yocto Project, NVIDIA Jetson Orin, cloud infrastructure, or Electron, React, and TypeScript. **About You** You are a hands-on engineering student who wants to understand how software behaves on real hardware. You work methodically, seek out missing knowledge, communicate clearly, and care about building tools and systems that others can use. **Required Skills** - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related engineering discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028. - Ability to work onsite in Pittsburgh, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship. - Foundational programming experience in C/C++ and Python, including object-oriented programming. - Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems. - Understanding of basic computer networking. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work, explain findings and tradeoffs, and collaborate on ambiguous problems. - Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback. **Preferred Skills** - Experience with ROS 2. - Familiarity with embedded Linux systems or platforms such as the Yocto Project or NVIDIA Jetson Orin. - Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP. - Experience building applications with Electron, React, or TypeScript. - Exposure to embedded communication protocols, microcontrollers, or real-time operating systems is a plus. - Ability to work with basic electronic systems, read simple schematics, and use common lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, and programmable power supplies. # **Who We Are** At Gecko, our people are our greatest investment. In addition to competitive compensation packages, we offer company equity, 401(k) matching, gender-neutral parental leave, full medical, dental, and vision insurance, mental health, ongoing professional development, family planning assistance, and flexible paid time off. Gecko values collaboration, innovation, and partnership, and we believe we do our best work when we're together in person. We’re an office-first culture but understand that sometimes you may need to work from home. Many people are in the office five days a week, others need a bit more flexibility. Ultimately, we care about the outcomes we achieve - and creating a culture of autonomy and trust that enables that impact. Gecko is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission to protect today’s infrastructure and give form to tomorrow’s. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our critical mission, we’d love to hear from you.

# **What We Do** Gecko Robotics is helping the world’s most important organizations ensure the availability, reliability, and sustainability of critical infrastructure. Gecko's complete and connected solutions combine wall-climbing robots, industry-leading sensors, and an AI-powered data platform to provide customers with a unique window into the current and future health of their physical assets. This enables real-time decision making to increase the efficiency and safety of operations, promote mission readiness, and protect the environment and civilization from the effects of infrastructure failure. ## **Role at a Glance** Gecko Robotics is seeking a **Test & Reliability Engineer Intern** to join Field Infra’s Test & Reliability (T&R) team in Pittsburgh for **Summer 2027**. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday. You will contribute to a defined engineering project focused on making our robotic systems more dependable by building software tools, automating tests, and analyzing system data and logs. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will develop practical tools, execute tests, and generate evidence that improves how Gecko validates and learns from its robotic systems. **What you will do** - Own a scoped engineering project that improves a test, regression, reliability-analysis, or test-data workflow. - Help plan, execute, and document software and integrated robotic-system tests under the guidance of experienced engineers. - Analyze test results, clearly document findings and open questions, and recommend improvements to test coverage and repeatability. - Develop or improve tooling, automation, scripts, or documentation that makes testing more efficient and reliable. - Collaborate with Test & Reliability engineers and partner teams to understand how field observations and engineering requirements inform validation. - Present your project, results, and recommended next steps at the end of the internship. **Technologies We Use** Depending on the assigned project, you may work with Python, Linux, Git, hardware and software test equipment, data-analysis tools, and robotic-system logs. The specific tools and technologies will depend on the assigned project. **About You** You are a curious, hands-on engineering student who enjoys understanding how complex systems behave in the real world. You are comfortable learning across software and hardware boundaries, approaching problems methodically, and communicating what you observed and what you do not yet know. **Required Skills** - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering, computer science, robotics, or a related technical discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028. - Ability to work onsite in Pittsburgh, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship. - Foundational programming experience in Python or another general-purpose programming language. - Experience writing, testing, or debugging software through coursework, projects, research, competition teams, or a prior internship. - Interest in software testing, reliability, robotics, embedded systems, or complex physical systems. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to structure technical problems, document work clearly, communicate findings, and learn from feedback. **Preferred Skills** - Previous hands-on experience with robotics, embedded systems, electronics, mechanical systems, or other complex physical systems through an internship, research position, engineering lab, competition team, or substantial project. - Experience using Python to automate test workflows or analyze system data, logs, or failures. - Familiarity with Linux, Git, and structured testing or debugging practices. - Experience designing experiments, debugging system behavior, or building tools for others. - Coursework or projects in software testing, controls, mechatronics, reliability engineering, systems engineering, or a related field. # **Who We Are** At Gecko, our people are our greatest investment. In addition to competitive compensation packages, we offer company equity, 401(k) matching, gender-neutral parental leave, full medical, dental, and vision insurance, mental health, ongoing professional development, family planning assistance, and flexible paid time off. Gecko values collaboration, innovation, and partnership, and we believe we do our best work when we're together in person. We’re an office-first culture but understand that sometimes you may need to work from home. Many people are in the office five days a week, others need a bit more flexibility. Ultimately, we care about the outcomes we achieve - and creating a culture of autonomy and trust that enables that impact. Gecko is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission to protect today’s infrastructure and give form to tomorrow’s. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our critical mission, we’d love to hear from you.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Our Flight Engineering department is divided into three critical areas: Flight Software (FSW), Guidance, Navigation & Control (GNC), and Modeling, Simulation & Analysis (MSA). U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. - Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in one of our offices in summer 2027. **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS** - A strong foundation in software development (for FSW candidates), control theory (for GNC candidates), or analytical modeling (for MSA candidates). - Keen interest in autonomous systems, UAS, and missile technology. - Excellent communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills. - Hands-on experience with Design-Build-Fly teams, robotics competition teams (such as FIRST or VEX), or collegiate rocketry groups. - Credible demonstration of aerospace-related hobbies such as high-power rocketry experience/certification, remotely piloted/semi-autonomous aircraft, or software integration on target hardware such as Raspberry Pi, Pixhawk, CubePilot (such as Cube Orange), or custom microcontrollers, using onboard IMU, GNSS, and Flight Simulation, Software-in-the-Loop (SITL) or Hardware-in-the-Loop (HITL) simulation environments. - Experience with open-source autopilot software suites like ArduPilot or PX4. - Experience with integrating flight hardware components including servos/actuators, IMUs, magnetometers, GNSS receivers and antennas, and serial communication protocols (such as UART, CAN, I2C, SPI) or radio telemetry links. - Basic familiarity with electrical test equipment (such as multimeters or oscilloscopes) and post-flight data analysis using tools like Python or MATLAB. description: **Datadog AI Research — Scholars Program with Carnegie Mellon University** Datadog AI Research (DAIR) is partnering with Carnegie Mellon University to support a small number of PhD students working on open research problems grounded by ongoing efforts at Datadog/DAIR. You will frame a problem, run your own experiments, and write up what you find, with compute and data at a scale most academic labs cannot provide. You will collaborate with colleagues working on the same questions. **The Lab And The Research:** DAIR is an industrial research lab motivated by practical challenges in observability and software operation: detecting and diagnosing failures, understanding complex production environments, and helping engineers operate software more effectively. The lab focuses on creating specialized foundation models, post-training and evaluating AI agents, and building frontier-scale machine learning systems. By combining fundamental research with Datadog's large-scale, real-world data and infrastructure, the lab develops new AI capabilities and translates them into practical systems with meaningful impact. Internship projects are shaped with your DAIR mentor and your CMU faculty advisor.
