**IMPORTANT:** in the application form, please specify what term you would like to begin your internship (winter/summer/fall) # **ABOUT ABUNDANT** AI models rely on two fundamental ingredients: compute and data. *Abundant is building the NVIDIA of training data.* NVIDIA, the leader in compute, has a peak market cap of $5T and generated $130B in revenue last year as the need for scaling compute has exploded. We believe the need to scale data is just beginning, as we move beyond SFT and human supervision to RL and Learning from Experience. Our founding team consists of former founders, ML engineers, roboticists and data leads from Waymo, Google, Mercor and AWS. Our team has previously worked with DeepMind to deploy deep learning models at 1B user scale, trained SOTA models for self-driving at Waymo, and scaled data pipelines of tens of thousands of human annotators at YouTube. Our pioneering work in human computation, synthetic data, simulation and RL give us the advantage in delivering results to our customers. Why now? Training data is more important and more scarce than ever before. Scaling laws dictate that linear improvement in model performance demands an exponential increase in training data. But there is only one World Wide Web and most of it has already been trained on. The next advances will require major advances in simulation, synthetic data and learning from experience. What happens if we succeed? Abundant will be the core enabler for not only AGI, but ASI and physical intelligence. Most of the challenges in model algorithms and compute are already solved. What’s missing? The data necessary to move from general knowledge to domain expertise; from chatbots to agents; and from text to multimodal and physical AI. Ask any AI researcher or roboticist: the core bottleneck to progress is the availability of data, hence “*abundant data*”. Abundant works with a majority of the top AI labs, as well as frontier startups and F500 enterprises. # **THE ROLE** As a Member of Technical Staff, you will work directly with Abundant's founding team to architect the next generation of model reasoning and intelligence. You will lead at the absolute frontier where research and execution collide, co-designing strategies alongside top-tier researchers from AI labs to push SOTA boundaries. This is a role for a extremely strong engineers who are already contributing frontier research. # **WHAT YOU’LL DO** - **Drive Foundational Research & Execution**: Architect and execute a core research agenda to discover simple, generalizable ideas that advance model reasoning and intelligence at scale. This includes owning the full research-to-production lifecycle and ensuring rapid deployment of your work in live systems. - **Model Alignment & Data Strategy**: Partner with the world's most advanced AI research teams to design, engineer, and iterate on high-impact datasets and large-scale benchmarking efforts that shape how frontier models behave, specifically focusing on critical alignment, safety, and defining optimal reward signals. - **Autonomous Problem Selection**: Autonomously identify, scope, and manage long-running research projects, choosing the most impactful problems that are critical to scaling data for AGI/ASI. - **System Infrastructure**: Collaborate closely with engineering teams on data pipelines, internal tooling, and high-performance deep learning algorithm implementations. # **WHO YOU ARE** - **Exceptional Research Depth & Strategic Vision**: Research expertise in a related field (e.g., CS, ML, NLP) ideally with that work published at a major conference (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR). You must possess the velocity to master complex fields and a proven track record in the productization of research, encompassing high-stakes evaluation, large-scale benchmarking, and product feature development. - Proven experience shipping research directly to production and live systems, specifically focusing on advanced post-training, distillation, and high-stakes evaluation methodologies. - Large-scale agent systems: orchestration frameworks, tool APIs, distributed execution, observability, and logging infrastructure. - **Strategic & Ethical Leadership**: You possess a thoughtful, strategic perspective on the societal and safety impacts of deploying general-purpose AI systems. Experience advising on or shaping governmental policy related to AI safety and governance (e.g., House of Lords or Online Safety Bill initiatives) is required. # **COMPENSATION** **Base Salary** $10,000/month **Benefits** Health, dental, vision + flexible PTO

role: KIP Spring 2027 - Strategic Research Intern - Pacific Legal Foundation
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! ### **General Information** Pacific Legal Foundation identifies and litigates important legal issues to set landmark precedents that benefit Americans nationwide. Using strategic and principled litigation, communications, and research, PLF battles for freedom in the nation’s courts and the court of public opinion. As a national nonprofit organization, PLF has brick-and-mortar offices in Sacramento, California; Arlington, Virginia; and Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, although approximately half of the staff work from home offices across the country. **Interns work remotely by default, but they can request to work physically in any of PLF’s offices. This is a part-time role.** **You:** An inquisitive, creative, and self-motivated college junior, senior, grad student, or recent graduate who knows the principles of liberty and seeks to advance them. You have strong written and oral communication skills and enjoy problem solving. **Them:** Bureaucrats, city councils, mayors, governors, and federal agencies stripping Americans of their rights every day. There’s a lot of government overreach out there, and it’s backed by seemingly endless resources. **Us:** We fight back. [Pacific Legal Foundation (PLF)](https://pacificlegal.org/) is the nation’s first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to vindicating individual liberty. PLF has an unmatched record in the US Supreme Court, with 18 victories out of 20 cases heard by the Court. PLF also has nearly 200 active cases across the nation. At PLF, we aren’t interested in doing the same thing as everyone else. We aspire to be the best player in a constantly changing game. The Strategic Research intern will be a member of the Strategic Research team. This team produces high-quality social science research to support PLF’s mission-driven goals. The team coordinates with PLF’s Litigation, Legal Policy, Constitutional Scholarship, and Communications teams. This internship is an opportunity for a wide variety of experiences, including the following: · Communicating with public officials to obtain public records. · Collecting, organizing, and analyzing data using Microsoft Excel, R, Python, GIS, or Stata. · Conducting literature reviews on such topics as regulatory reform, housing supply, property rights, coastal land rights, and more. · Developing internal data for litigation, communications, or legal policy campaigns. · Writing blog posts, op-eds, or one-pagers on topics relevant to PLF’s work. ### How to Apply **If you think you might be a good fit, submit the following application materials in ONE PDF when you upload your** **résumé that includes relevant experience in the liberty movement and professional skills:** · A cover letter explaining why PLF is the place for you, why you want to fight for liberty, and what distinguishes you from typical applicants. · A writing sample. · A semester schedule (if taking classes during the internship period).

description: Immuta is the Data Authorization Company, helping the world’s largest organizations control who, and what, can access their data. The way enterprises access data is fundamentally changing. Organizations are racing to put data to work across analytics and AI, while AI copilots and agents are emerging as an entirely new class of data consumer. Traditional approaches built around tickets, static permissions, and manual approvals were not designed for this speed, scale, or complexity. Immuta provides the authorization layer for modern data and AI. Our platform enables organizations to provision governed access to data by policy, by request, and dynamically for AI agents, so people and AI can access the data they need while enterprises maintain security, compliance, and control. For Chief Data Officers, that means making enterprise data dramatically easier to access and use without giving up governance. For AI leaders, it means giving AI agents secure, governed access to enterprise data so they can move from experimentation into production. Founded in 2015, Immuta is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies worldwide. - Our technology ecosystem includes Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Okta, ServiceNow, Teradata, Alation, Atlan, and Starburst — connecting Immuta to the data, cloud, identity, and enterprise platforms powering modern data and AI environments. - Immuta has been recognized by Forbes as a top American startup employer, by Inc. Magazine and Built In as one of the best workplaces, and by Fast Company as one of the world’s most innovative companies. - Immuta has raised $263 million from investors including NightDragon, Snowflake, Databricks, ServiceNow, Citi Ventures, Dell Technologies Capital, DFJ Growth, IAG, Intel Capital, March Capital, Okta Ventures, StepStone, Ten Eleven Ventures, and Wipro Ventures. - We operate as a hybrid workplace with offices in Boston, MA; Columbus, OH; and College Park, MD. ## **ABOUT THE TEAM** UX Design at Immuta helps make complex data access and governance workflows easier to understand and use. The team brings together design, research, and engineering to understand user problems, explore solutions, and turn them into clear, usable product experiences. As a UX Design Intern, you’ll work with UX designers and collaborate with product and engineering teammates. You’ll help connect customer needs to what the product actually does and learn how a product team moves from understanding a problem to designing and prototyping a solution. ## **YOUR INTERNSHIP** At Immuta, interns are treated like members of the team. You’ll join the team’s regular workflow, contribute to real work, and take on responsibilities that reflect your skills and the team’s priorities. The exact projects will depend on what the team is working on next summer, but you can expect to: - Explore user and customer problems through research, conversations, workshops, and other discovery activities. - Turn research and product insights into concepts, user flows, mockups, and prototypes. - Use design tools to communicate ideas, explain design decisions, and gather feedback. - Work with engineers and product teammates to understand constraints and shape solutions that can work in the real product. - Participate in activities such as storyboarding, journey mapping, user interviews, and portfolio or design critiques. - Use front-end skills, where relevant, to prototype, test, or communicate how an experience could work across responsive and mobile interfaces. - Share your work, explain your thinking, incorporate feedback, and build confidence working across design, research, and engineering. ## **TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES** Depending on your role, you may work with: - Figma and similar design tools - Wireframing, mockups, and interactive prototyping - Storyboarding, journey mapping, user interviews, and other research methods - HTML and CSS - Front-end frameworks such as Angular or React - Responsive and mobile design concepts - AI-enabled tools and workflows used by your team You do not need to know every tool listed above. We’re looking for a strong foundation, curiosity, and the ability to learn. ## **WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR** - A portfolio that demonstrates your design work, prototypes, research, product thinking, or other relevant projects. - Strong ability in at least one of three areas: visual design, user research, or engineering/front-end development. Experience across two or more is a plus. - You do not need to be equally strong in all three areas. We’re interested in candidates who can demonstrate clear strength in at least one and curiosity about the others. - Curiosity about users, products, and how technology can solve real problems. - Strong communication and collaboration skills. - Initiative, willingness to learn, and comfort receiving and applying feedback.

# **Chart Your Journey at Secretariat** From a collaborative culture to teammates who will always be by your side, find a career that will grow with you. Deliver your impact at Secretariat. **ABOUT THE FIRM** Secretariat is a consulting firm that helps companies, law firms, and organizations solve complex business problems—often when there is a dispute, investigation, major project challenge, or high-stakes decision involved. At Secretariat, you’ll work on some of the most important legal, risk, and regulatory challenges facing businesses around the world. From your first day, you’ll be part of a fast-growing team of smart, curious, and driven people who enjoy solving complex problems. You’ll learn by working alongside experienced professionals and contributing to projects for leading law firms, global companies, and major institutions. Our teams collaborate across offices and disciplines, bringing energy, fresh thinking, and commitment to every client challenge. We invest in your growth through hands-on experience, mentorship, professional development, recognition, and a culture that values diverse perspectives. Start your career where your work matters. Make your impact at Secretariat. **ABOUT OUR ENGINEERING SCIENCES TEAM** As part of our growing Global Engineering Sciences team, you’ll apply what you’re learning in the classroom to real-world engineering challenges across industries such as energy, chemicals, machinery, automotive, consumer products, electronics, medical devices, and the built environment. You may help investigate why products, systems, or structures fail, support testing and analysis, and contribute to projects involving buildings, bridges, industrial facilities, and other structures that shape the world around us. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers, scientists, and consultants to learn how engineering is used to solve complex questions related to performance, safety, reliability, and design. This is a great fit for students who are curious, analytical, and excited to build practical technical and consulting skills. Secretariat is a fast-growing international expert services firm with more than 500 professionals in 20+ cities worldwide. For students and early-career professionals, we offer meaningful work from day one, mentorship from leading experts, and the chance to build valuable technical, consulting, and problem-solving skills. **RESPONSIBILITIES** In this role, you’ll build practical engineering, analytical, and consulting skills by supporting real client projects from investigation through reporting. You’ll work with experienced professionals who will help you learn how to break down complex technical questions, analyze information, and communicate your findings clearly. - Support hands-on failure investigations and learn how engineers evaluate what happened, why it happened, and how it can be explained clearly. - Compare real-world conditions with original designs, drawings, specifications, and project documents. - Assist with field inspections, site visits, laboratory testing, and other investigative activities. - Perform engineering calculations, research technical issues, and analyze data to help solve complex problems. - Review, organize, and summarize project documents, technical records, photos, test results, and other relevant information. - Help draft clear, well-supported report sections that explain technical findings in a way clients can understand. - Contribute to visuals, exhibits, and demonstratives that help tell the story of a technical issue or investigation. - Analyze technical reports prepared by others and help develop supporting, concurring, or rebuttal perspectives. - Participate in team and client communications, gaining exposure to consulting work across different industries and time zones. - Build strong working relationships with colleagues, peers, and clients while contributing to a collaborative team environment. - Use curiosity, attention to detail, and strong analytical thinking to help the team meet project milestones and deliver high-quality work. **QUALIFICATIONS** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Building Science/Architectural Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree candidates are also encouraged to apply. - Expected graduation date between December 2027 and August 2030. - Minimum GPA of 3.0. - Interest in pursuing PE credentials is a plus. - Curious, analytical, and eager to solve complex problems in practical, real-world settings. - Strong communication skills, including listening, writing, presenting, and explaining technical ideas clearly. - Able to learn quickly, think creatively, manage competing priorities, and ask thoughtful questions when guidance is needed. - Comfortable working both independently and as part of a collaborative team in a fast-growing consulting environment. - Proficiency with Microsoft Office, especially Excel and PowerPoint. - Willingness and ability to travel as needed. - Additional language skills are a plus. - Authorized to work in the U.S. without current or future sponsorship. ## A rewarding career above all There are a lot of fine consulting firms out there. But when everything is on the line, it takes a unique combination of skill and savvy to succeed under pressure. Our culture and people are driven by passion, pride, and performance. Passion for the clients we serve, the work we deliver, and the communities we live in. Pride in our cohesive team recognized for excellence and trusted to perform in the most challenging situations. And our track record of outstanding performance across all of our disciplines speaks for itself. [Our people](https://secretariat-intl.com/people/) are motivated to be the best in everything they do – from our approach to making the complex simple to the way we mentor our up-and-coming talent to become trusted experts early in their careers. description: ISW Internship Program Overview ISW is offering in-person, remote, and hybrid internships for Spring 2027. Instructions to apply for the scholarship are below. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) is committed to training the next generation of national security leaders through its innovative educational programs. ISW seeks motivated and experienced college students or recent graduates to join our intern team. ISW offers internships across diverse research portfolios and departments, including Russia, China, and Iran's Axis of Resistance. ISW also offers internships in Geospatial Intelligence and National Security Technologies, our Cognitive Warfare Task Force, and in Communications. Why Work for ISW? ISW believes that ground realities must drive the formulation of strategy and policy. In pursuit of this principle, ISW conducts detailed open-source intelligence analysis to provide timely and accurate information on current conflicts and security threats directly to policymakers and warfighters. Interns at ISW have an unparalleled opportunity to analyze conflicts in ways that directly inform policymakers on some of the most pressing issues facing American national security. Our interns work directly with analysts. They receive classroom education, regular leadership engagement, and a chance to work with cutting-edge technologies employed in business and the intelligence community. Interns have the opportunity to stand at the front lines of military research and policy development, tackling the latest crises in the headlines. The ISW Internship Program is one of three core education programs housed within The General David H. Petraeus Center for Emerging Leaders, launched to identify, educate, and develop the future cadre of leaders committed to America’s national security. ISW views interns as an integral component of its team. ISW has worked with interns to draft, edit, and publish their own research under the mentorship of senior analysts. It has also hired many interns onto its staff. Russia Occupation Research Internship : ISW is a leading source of innovative analysis and intelligence on global conflicts that threaten American national security. ISW publishes regular research reports and graphics to inform US and international policy-makers, warfighters, and journalists in Washington, DC, as well as the general public. Interns provide critical assistance to our analysts and receive hands-on training from their supervisors as well as a formal development program taught by our leadership. Interns will be trained to use innovative technologies to conduct open-source collection and analysis in a fast-paced environment. Interns will support ISW's Russian Occupation Update product line and related research efforts, which examine the implications of Russian occupation strategy, governance policy, and coercive apparatus in Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine. Interns will be expected to collect, process, and analyze data from a wide-variety of open-sources and write sections of the Russian Occupation Update to publishable ISW standard. Interns will also support longer-term research efforts focusing on occupation administration, repression, sociocultural control, administrative integration, and the humanitarian and human rights implications of the occupation. Over the course of this internship, interns will develop a rigorous understanding of how military occupations are enacted and enforced, and how adversaries use occupation as a tool of influence and demographic management. This is a full-time internship (five days per week), but part-time work may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Qualifications Candidates must have a demonstrated interest in war studies, national security, or regional studies, particularly related to Russia, Ukraine, Eastern Europe, and the post-Soviet space. Candidates must also have a demonstrated interest in military occupations, irregular warfare and coercive activities, humanitarian and human rights issues in conflict zones, and international and human rights law. Candidates should preferably possess strong reading and listening comprehension in Russian and/or Ukrainian. Candidates must possess strong analytical writing, editing, research, and communication skills. Candidates must be self-motivated, detail-oriented, independent, and capable of working in a constantly changing and fast-paced professional environment. Candidates should have demonstrated professional or academic experience in using foreign languages (preferably Russian and/or Ukrainian) to conduct primary source research. Competitive candidates should also have professional or academic familiarity with open-source intelligence methodologies, including analysis of social media sources, government statements, satellite imagery, and local-level reporting. Experience with mapping and data visualization and organization tools is also a plus. Candidates must show commitment to—and interest in—the core mission and values of ISW. Spring 2027 Internship Program Dates: ISW internships starts on September 8, 2026 . The program will run until December 11 . Interns must both be authorized to work in the United States and be physically present in the United States during their internship tenure. Working remotely outside of the United States is not authorized. If you attend a US university on a student visa, you must be eligible for and obtain a CPT authorization before beginning at ISW. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Instructions: Please upload your resume, cover letter, and writing sample. Your cover letter and writing sample should be no longer than five pages combined; the writing sample can be excerpted from a longer paper. ISW will work with students to gain academic credit for internships where applicable. ISW Scholarship Application The Institute for the Study of War will offer intern candidates up to a $1,000 monthly living stipend as part of a scholarship program.* To be considered for the scholarship, candidates must upload a scholarship application as part of their internship application. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Candidates will be assessed based on the following criteria: Ability to contribute as a member of one of ISW’s research, operations, business development, or external relations teams; and Financial need, such that an unpaid internship would not be possible without assistance. Within the scholarship application, candidates should upload a 2- to 3-page cover letter which answers each of the following questions. (This should be a different cover letter than the one used for the internship application itself.) Which ISW internship is your top choice? Why do you believe you are qualified? What do you believe to be the most pressing national security problem the US faces today? What solution(s) would you propose? Where do you see yourself in your future career? How will an ISW internship help you get there? Why have you chosen to apply for this supplemental scholarship? Are you currently receiving federal financial aid and/or need-based aid from your university? Feel free to describe using as much detail as you are comfortable. *Please note that the up to $1,000 monthly scholarship is classified as taxable income. Questions? Email for more information.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit [](https://shield.ai/). Follow Shield AI on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai), [X](https://x.com/shieldaitech), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai), and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI). Our Summer Internship program is a wonderful opportunity for Fall and Spring graduates to immerse themselves in an innovative and mission driven culture. Our paid internship program will provide you with hands on mentorship, an opportunity to add real contribution to our company via your internship project, and a possible job offer at the end. You will have the chance to make lifelong friendships, expand your network, and learn all about what it's like to work in a high-growth, fast scaling tech unicorn. You'll take part in company sponsored events and enjoy exploring a new city. Read on below to learn more about this unique internship! ### About the Role Shield AI's Software Development Engineer Intern program spans engineers who design, build, and test the code that powers our autonomous systems — from user-facing applications and embedded flight software to machine learning models and the underlying systems platforms that tie it all together. Over 10–12 weeks, interns work alongside full-time engineers to analyze requirements, write and debug production-quality code, and ship a real feature or capability using our standard Agile development practices. **Example Intern Projects** - **Applications:** Build a new feature or internal tool (web, mobile, or desktop) that streamlines a mission-planning or fleet-management workflow. - **Firmware/Embedded:** Develop and debug embedded C/C++ code for a flight controller or sensor module, including bring-up and hardware-in-the-loop testing. - **Machine Learning:** Train, evaluate, and integrate a perception or decision-making model (e.g., object detection, sensor fusion) into an autonomy pipeline. - **Systems Development:** Extend a platform tool, API, or data pipeline that supports autonomy software, simulation, or cloud infrastructure. ### Required Qualifications - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field - Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., C, C++, Python, Java, or JavaScript) - Solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, and software design principles - Experience writing, testing, and debugging code, whether through coursework, personal projects, or prior internships - Familiarity with version control (e.g., Git) and collaborative development workflows - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down ambiguous requirements into working code - Effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment ### Preferred Qualifications - Exposure to mobile or web application frameworks and full-stack development - Hands-on experience with embedded systems, microcontrollers, real-time operating systems, or assembly-level debugging - Coursework or projects involving machine learning, statistics, probability theory, or deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) - Experience with cloud platforms, databases, networking, or distributed systems - Familiarity with Agile/Scrum development methodologies - Prior internship, research, or club/competition experience in robotics, autonomy, or aerospace applications - Interest in or exposure to the defense, aerospace, or autonomous systems industry

description: The General Laborer performs a variety of manual labor and production support duties throughout the pipe foundry. This position assists in the manufacturing, handling, inspection, finishing, and movement of cast iron pipe and related products while maintaining a safe and productive work environment. Employees may be assigned to various departments based on operational needs and seniority in accordance with the collective bargaining agreement. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Perform general labor tasks in support of foundry and pipe manufacturing operations. Assist with molding, melting, casting, finishing, cleaning, coating, and shipping processes. Handle, move, stack, and prepare materials, castings, and finished products. Operate basic production equipment and tools following established procedures and training. Inspect products for defects and notify supervision of quality concerns. Remove excess material, grind castings, clean work areas, and perform finishing operations. Assist operators, maintenance personnel, and production teams as needed. Load and unload materials, supplies, and finished products. Maintain housekeeping standards and keep work areas clean and organized. Follow production schedules and work instructions to meet quality and productivity standards. Comply with all safety policies, procedures, and work rules. Wear required personal protective equipment (PPE) at all times. Operational tasks in compliance with established Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures to ensure the safe isolation of hazardous energy sources before servicing, maintaining, or entering equipment. Perform other duties as assigned within the scope of the bargaining unit classification. Safety Responsibilities Follow all company safety policies, procedures, and work rules. Properly use and maintain required personal protective equipment (PPE). Comply with all Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures and hazardous energy control requirements. Immediately report unsafe conditions, incidents, near misses, and injuries. Participate in required safety training, meetings, and audits. Maintain a clean and orderly work area to support a safe work environment. Key Competencies Safety Awareness Dependability Teamwork Work Ethic Attention to Quality Adaptability Initiative Communication Skills Required Ability to perform physically demanding work in an industrial environment. Ability to read and follow work instructions and safety procedures. Ability to work effectively as part of a team. Reliable attendance and punctuality. Preferred High School Diploma or GED Manufacturing, foundry, construction, warehouse, or industrial experience. Forklift, overhead crane, or industrial equipment experience. Experience working in a union manufacturing environment. Physical Requirements Ability to stand and walk for extended periods during the shift. Ability to frequently bend, stoop, squat, kneel, push, pull, and climb. Ability to lift, carry, and move materials weighing up to 50 pounds regularly and heavier loads with assistance. Ability to perform repetitive tasks using hands and arms. Ability to demonstrate full upper body range of motion, including reaching overhead, reaching forward, extending arms, and performing tasks requiring shoulder, arm, wrist, and hand mobility. Ability to work overtime, weekends, holidays, and various shifts as required by operations and the collective bargaining agreement. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Are you a technology-minded student who enjoys solving business challenges and improving team member experience? You'll make a meaningful impact by helping improve the tools and systems that support our team members while being mentored by experienced People Technology professionals. In this role, you will be an integral part of our People Technology team. Your key responsibility will be to support the ongoing optimization and adoption of Workday and other HR technologies by gathering feedback, analyzing system usage, and identifying opportunities for improvement. You will work closely with business partners and technical teams to help ensure our people systems deliver a seamless employee experience from hire to retire. What You’ll Do Support People Technology initiatives: Help evaluate and improve the systems and technologies that support team members across the organization, including Workday and other HR platforms. Gather and analyze user feedback: Partner with business functions and field teams to identify pain points, assess user adoption, and understand how employees interact with people technologies. Drive data-informed recommendations: Analyze system usage, processes, and feedback to identify opportunities for enhancements, improved governance, and stronger data quality. Collaborate across teams: Work closely with business partners, HR functions, and IT teams to support technology solutions that improve the overall employee experience. What We’re Looking For Education: Currently pursuing an undergraduate degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Data Science, Business Technology, Management Information Systems, or a related field. Technical Skills: Proficiency in Excel and the Microsoft Office Suite is essential. Familiarity with system integrations or process mapping is highly valued. Experience with Visio, HCM systems, or Workday is a plus. Soft Skills: Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences. Demonstrated problem-solving abilities, curiosity, and the ability to collaborate effectively across multiple functions and teams. Qualities: A passion for technology and improving the employee experience. We value individuals who are driven, reliable, authentic, and welcoming. Why Pilot Company? Our culture is built on four core virtues: Driven, Reliable, Authentic, and Welcoming. As an intern, you will see these values in action every day. You'll be part of a team that is driven to improve technology experiences, reliable in supporting critical business systems, authentic in its partnerships across the organization, and welcoming to new ideas and perspectives. This is a full-time, in-person internship running from June 7 – August 13, 2027. You’ll be working alongside our team in our Knoxville headquarters, where you’ll have the opportunity to build meaningful relationships and experience the full scope of life at Pilot Company. How to Apply If you're ready to take on a challenging and rewarding internship with a leading company, please submit your application. The interview process will include a screening with a recruiter, a 30-minute virtual interview with two leaders on our People Technology team, followed by a potential final round interview with the teams senior leader. We look forward to hearing from you! Pilot Company is an industry-leading network of travel centers with more than 30,000 team members and over 750 retail and fueling locations in 44 states and six Canadian provinces. Our energy and logistics division serves as a top supplier of fuel, employing one of the largest tanker fleets and providing critical services to oil operations in our nation's busiest basins. Pilot Company supports a growing portfolio of brands with expertise in supply chain and retail operations, logistics and transportation, technology and digital innovation, construction, maintenance, human resources, finance, sales and marketing. Position Summary We are seeking a motivated Junior Commissioning & SCADA Engineer to support the commissioning, testing, and operational integration of utility-scale renewable energy facilities and electrical infrastructure. This role provides hands-on experience with SCADA systems, plant controls, commissioning activities, and NERC compliance while working alongside experienced engineering and field teams. The ideal candidate is an early-career electrical engineer who is eager to develop technical expertise in power systems, renewable energy, substation controls, and grid operations. Key Responsibilities Commissioning Support Assist with commissioning of utility-scale solar, BESS, substations, and related electrical infrastructure. Support pre-commissioning inspections, functional testing, energization, and turnover activities. Review commissioning procedures and verify completion of required documentation. Coordinate with EPC contractors, equipment vendors, utilities, and project teams during commissioning. Participate in startup, troubleshooting, and performance testing of electrical equipment. SCADA & Controls Support Assist with configuration, testing, and validation of SCADA systems. Support integration of inverters, protective relays, meters, RTUs, PLCs, and communications equipment. Help verify point-to-point testing between field devices and control centers. Troubleshoot communication issues involving fiber, Ethernet, serial communications, and industrial protocols. Support development and maintenance of SCADA documentation and system drawings. NERC Compliance Support Assist with maintaining documentation required for applicable NERC Reliability Standards. Support compliance audits, evidence collection, and record retention. Help track required testing, maintenance, and cybersecurity documentation. Work with operations and engineering teams to support ongoing compliance initiatives. Engineering Support Review electrical drawings, one-line diagrams, wiring diagrams, and control schematics. Assist with equipment inspections and field quality verification. Prepare commissioning reports and technical documentation. Support engineering evaluations and field issue resolution. Travel to project sites as required. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or closely related field. 0–3 years of engineering experience (internships or co-op experience welcomed). Understanding of electrical power systems. Basic knowledge of substations, renewable energy systems, or industrial controls preferred. Familiarity with SCADA systems or industrial communications is a plus. Exposure to protective relays, PLCs, RTUs, or power system automation is desirable. Knowledge of NERC Reliability Standards is preferred but not required. Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to travel approximately 30–50% to project sites.

Field Engineers play a key role in ensuring that work meets the required quality standards by conducting inspections and implementing quality control measures. - **Participation in Project Meetings:** Regular participation in both daily and weekly project meetings is necessary to stay updated on project progress, discuss issues, and coordinate activities with other team members. - **Document Management:** Ensuring that Field Superintendents and Foremen have access to up-to-date contract documents, drawings, specifications, submittals, RFIs, and shop drawings is crucial for keeping the project on track. - **Issue Reporting:** Field Engineers promptly report any field issues to the Project Engineer and Field Superintendent. This allows for swift problem resolution and minimizes delays. - **Quantity Tracking:** Field Engineers are responsible for tracking and reporting the quantities of installed materials and equipment on a weekly basis. This is essential for project cost control and progress assessment. - **Equipment and Material Management:** Managing the storage and maintenance of equipment and materials on-site is necessary to ensure that resources are readily available and in good condition. - **Record Drawings and As-Builts:** Maintaining accurate record drawings and as-builts as per contract requirements is important for future reference and documentation. - **Permit Document Maintenance:** Field Engineers may be responsible for managing permit documents, such as those related to dust control and stormwater pollution prevention (SWPPP). - **Project Progress Photos:** Gathering weekly project progress photos can help document the project's development and provide visual updates to project stakeholders. - **Training and Mentoring:** Field Engineers often play a role in, sharing their knowledge and expertise to help develop the next generation of professionals. - **Stakeholder Relations:** Building rapport with owners, clients, engineers, and trade partners is important. Field Engineers must also ensure that the project complies with all contractual obligations and requirements. **Qualifications** - Applicant must be currently enrolled in a four-year Construction Management or Engineering program. - Ability to assume responsibility, interface and effectively communicate with others - Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) - Positive and teachable attitude **Safety Level** This is a safety sensitive position, and all applicable policies including drug test and background check will apply. - The inherent responsibilities of your role may include physical working conditions. In order to safely and successfully perform job duties you must be able to: - Potentially lift up to 50 pounds - Potentially need to do repeated pushing, pulling, carrying, reaching (or working above shoulder), walking, standing, sitting, stooping, kneeling, bending, and climbing - Potentially operate a motor vehicle, crane, tractor, etc. - We reserve the right to continually monitor your ability to safely and successfully complete these inherent physical responsibilities and take action as deemed appropriate in accordance with the Americans with Disability Act (ADA) This internship will provide you with exposure to the construction and project management industry, allowing you to apply your classroom knowledge to real-world situations. You will gain hands-on experience, work with experienced professionals, and contribute to the success of our projects. We look forward to your active participation and contributions to our team during this internship program. role: Electrical Engineering Intern (B+P) - Hiring Event with AECOM - Arlington
description: AECOM is hosting an exclusive, invitation-only hiring event in Arlington on November 18-19, 2026. This is a great opportunity to learn and connect with AECOM for career opportunities starting Spring/Summer 2027. The event kicks off on Wednesday evening with a networking mixer from 6-8 pm, where you can hear from AECOM staff about various projects, career paths, and the company itself. You’ll also have the chance to meet other students, recent graduates, and AECOM professionals from across our business lines. On Thursday, interviews will take place at our Arlington office. This is a fantastic opportunity to learn about and connect with AECOM for early career opportunities. AECOM is seeking an Electrical Engineering Intern to be based in Arlington, VA . This position is expected to begin in Spring/Summer 2027. Internships at AECOM offer students in undergraduate and graduate programs the opportunity to gain valuable hands-on experience in engineering, design, and infrastructure projects that make a real-world impact. Interns work with cutting-edge technology, learn industry best practices, and collaborate with experienced professionals in a globally recognized firm. The program fosters both technical and professional skill development while providing networking opportunities that can enhance future career prospects. Additionally, AECOM’s dedication to innovation and sustainability enables interns to contribute to meaningful projects that help shape communities and the built environment. The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to: Build analytic and design skills. Conduct engineering design under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Create designs, calculations, sketches, diagrams, schematic drawings, and final working drawings under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Collect and analyzes data under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Uses computer software as a tool for solving basic engineering problems. Perform work in accordance with agreed upon budget and schedule under supervision. Design and document normal, standby and emergency power distribution systems. Design and document normal and emergency lighting systems for interior and exterior applications. Perform calculations to support designs. Work through all project design phases including construction administration. Work on varying project types and sizes including laboratories, educational facilities, office spaces, mission critical facilities, and cultural facilities. Work in a team environment. Minimum Requirements: Candidates must be pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Architectural Engineering, or related field and must have completed at least two of years of study. Candidates who have graduated with a Bachelor’s degree and plan to continue with the Master’s degree are eligible to apply for these positions. Recent graduates must have been enrolled in their bachelor’s degree in the most previous school term with an interest in pursuing an advanced degree in the same or similar discipline at the conclusion of the internship. Due to the nature of the work, U.S. Citizenship is required. Preferred Qualifications: Use AutoCAD and/or Revit for creating construction documents, sketches, etc. Knowledge of SKM and/or ETAP to perform electrical studies. Knowledge of AGi32 software to perform lighting calculations. Experience of design work for new construction and renovation projects. Prior internship experience utilizing drafting, surveying, and/or construction administration skills. Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position. Relocation assistance is not available for this position. This position requires a hybrid work schedule which includes office work in Arlington, VA. The selected candidate must be available to work in Arlington, VA. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment. role: Flight Operations & Airworthiness Engineering Intern - Spring/Summer/Fall 2027
description: Hermeus is a venture-backed defense aviation company reclaiming the lost art of rapid iterative prototyping to build the fastest aircraft in the world today. By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. We work with the Department of War to provide the high-speed capabilities our nation and its allies need to maintain a durable, asymmetric advantage. ### **About the Role:** As a Flight Operations & Airworthiness Engineering Intern at Hermeus, you will support the planning, development, and execution of flight operations and airworthiness activities for the Quarterhorse aircraft. This role is ideal for an engineering student with practical aviation experience who is interested in the cross functional intersection of flight operations, flight test, safety, and airworthiness. You will contribute to professional technical deliverables supporting military and civil airworthiness packages, assist with risk assessments and data analysis, and support strategic planning that will advance longer-term program objectives. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who can take ownership of complex, ambiguous problems; develop a path forward; and communicate clearly across internal and external teams. This internship offers direct exposure to the unique challenges of operating and certifying high-performance experimental aircraft in a fast-paced development environment. Spring: Around 16 weeks (January - April) Summer: Around 12 weeks (May - August) Fall: Around 16 weeks (September - December) ### Responsibilities: - Support the development of airworthiness, flight operations, and safety documentation for experimental aircraft operations. - Assist in preparing professional technical deliverables for military and civil airworthiness packages. - Support operational-risk analysis, including hazard identification, risk tracking, and management of operational constraints and mitigations. - Apply engineering fundamentals and statistical methods to assess operational data, characterize risk, and support envelope an operational expansion. - Collaborate with engineering, flight test, operations, and program teams to collect technical inputs and ensure airworthiness artifacts are accurate, complete, and traceable. - Independently identify and effectively communicate gaps, inefficiencies, and upcoming needs in flight operations and airworthiness processes. - Support longer-range planning by identifying work that advances programmatic milestones and airworthiness objectives well ahead of formal tasking. ### Requirements: - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, systems engineering, or a related STEM discipline. Undergraduate candidates should be in their junior or senior year of study; graduate students are also encouraged to apply. - Demonstrated interest in aviation, flight test, flight operations, or airworthiness. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to develop clear, professional technical documentation. - Strong mathematical and analytical skills, including the ability to organize, interpret, and draw conclusions from engineering or test data. - Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment with shifting priorities. - Demonstrated initiative and comfort working through ambiguous technical or operational problems without a fully defined path. - Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and commitment to safe operations. - GPA of 3.0 or above. ### Preferred Skills and Experience: - Manned or unmanned aircraft pilot experience or comparable flight experience. - Experience with experimental aircraft, flight test, aircraft maintenance, aviation safety, or airworthiness activities. - Experience designing, building, testing, or operating vehicles through internships, academic work, student teams, military service, or personal projects. - Familiarity with risk-management methods, safety assessments, reliability analysis, statistical analysis, or data-analysis tools. - Exposure to civil or military aviation regulations, certification processes, flight authorizations, or airworthiness documentation. - Experience developing technical reports, engineering analyses, test procedures, or operational documentation. - A strong desire to learn, seek feedback, and take on progressively greater responsibility.

The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) protects public health and the environment by supplying clean drinking water, collecting and treating wastewater, and reducing air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution. DEP is the largest combined municipal water and wastewater utility in the country, with nearly 6,000 employees. DEP delivers more than 1.1 billion gallons per day of the highest quality drinking water to 8.5 million NYC residents and more than 1 million people in Upstate New York, and has a wastewater conveyance and treatment system capable of processing over 1.3 billion gallons of wastewater per day to protect the environment and the city’s surrounding waterways. The primary responsibilities of the Bureau of Water and Sewer Operations (BWSO) are: the operation, maintenance and protection of the City’s drinking water and wastewater collection (sewer) systems; the protection of adjacent waterways; and the development and protection of the Department’s Capital Water and Sewer Design Program. The Bureau also approves and inspects water and sewer connections performed by licensed plumbers and/or authorized contractors. In addition, the Bureau has overall responsibility for the approval and inspection of all public and private construction projects which could impact on the City’s water or sewer systems. The Bureau of Water and Sewer Operations is seeking to hire an Environmental Engineer Intern within the Division of Capital Program Management (CPM) for Distribution & Drainage section. The selected candidate will provide engineering support for stormwater management, drainage infrastructure, sewer systems, environmental compliance, and related water quality and resiliency projects. Responsibilities will include assisting with engineering analyses, data collection and evaluation, preparation of technical reports, review of design documents, and coordination with internal and external stakeholders. The employee will support the evaluation of drainage and sewer system through field investigations, hydraulic/environmental data review and modeling, GIS mapping, and engineering calculations. The position will assist senior engineers with: - Collecting, organizing, and analyzing environmental, hydraulic, and infrastructure-related data. - Supporting stormwater management and drainage improvement projects. - Reviewing drainage plans, reports, calculations, and technical documentation. - Performing basic engineering analyses and calculations. - Preparing spreadsheets, maps, figures, presentations, and technical reports. - Using engineering software, databases, GIS applications, and agency data management tools. - Participating in field visits to observe infrastructure conditions, collect information, and support project assessments. - Coordinating with DEP units, consultants, contractors, and other agencies as needed. The position provides an opportunity to gain practical experience in environmental engineering, stormwater management, drainage systems, and infrastructure planning while working under the guidance of experienced engineers. **ALL APPLICANTS MUST HAVE TAKEN CIVIL SERVICE EXAM NO. 6118 FOR ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEER INTERN, TO BE CONSIDERED FOR THIS POSITION. ** Appointments are subject to OMB approval. ## About Vercel: Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience. Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide. ## About the Role: As an Engineering Intern at Vercel, you will be an important part of our engineering team, working on real projects that will impact our products and customers. Collaborating with our experienced water professionals, you will support and drive the development of projects, interact and work with clients, and develop your technical capabilities. Your expertise will be essential in gathering critical data and ensuring the efficient and effective functioning of water and wastewater systems. You will also play a crucial role in supporting Asset Management projects. This will involve utilizing data analytics to perform operational and organizational assessments, conducting condition assessments, and evaluating the overall performance of water/wastewater/stormwater facilities. By providing valuable insights, you will contribute to improving asset management strategies and enhancing the overall performance of these systems. From coffee to lumber, every product we use has been traded through a complex supply chain of suppliers, manufacturers, wholesalers, and retailers. Despite the massive scale of this market, most businesses manage their trading relationships and commerce activities using outdated methods like paper forms, PDFs, emails, faxes, phone calls, and spreadsheets, making processes slow and inefficient. Much like how Shopify, Stripe and Square have transformed how consumer companies transact, we aim to do the same for B2B companies. ## About the Role We are looking for smart engineers to help build category-defining products. If you are driven, passionate, collaborative, hands on, and want to grow your technical skills – join us and help enable our expansion into the solar system. **Internship Disciplines** - Mechanical Test Engineering - Motor Control Engineering **About You** You’re a successful candidate if you are a giver, not a taker and have a desire to support your team in all the areas to mission success. ### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. ### **About the Software Integration Team** Are you excited about learning how complex software systems come together to power real-world autonomy? At Zipline, we operate the world’s largest autonomous delivery network, and our Software Integration team plays a critical role in making sure the software that flies our aircraft works reliably and safely in the real world. As a Software Integration Intern, you’ll get hands-on experience at the intersection of robotics, embedded software, and systems engineering. Our team doesn’t just write code—we bring together planning, perception, and controls software, and make sure all of it works smoothly on the aircraft, in simulation, and in real operations. You’ll help test and integrate features that affect how our autonomous aircraft fly, adapt routes, and respond to unexpected situations. That means working with simulation tools, flight telemetry, and testing infrastructure to ensure new software behaves the way it should before it ever goes into the sky. This internship is a chance to learn how large, safety-critical autonomy systems are built and scaled, while contributing to technology that directly impacts communities around the world. ### **The Role** We are seeking a Software Integration Intern with an interest in applying technical and engineering skills to real-world problems. The ideal candidate is eager to learn how to use data science and programming to support hardware systems integration and engineering projects. This internship provides the opportunity to work with large datasets, gain exposure to modern data tools, and apply engineering principles to create actionable insights. Familiarity with Python, SQL, and basic software development is helpful, but a strong willingness to learn is most important. ### **What You'll Do** - **Data Analysis & Modeling:** Assist in analyzing datasets from engineering systems, vehicle sensors, and other sources to uncover patterns and support predictive modeling efforts. - **Data Visualization:** Help design clear and visually appealing charts and dashboards using tools such as Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, or Tableau to communicate findings. - **Dashboard Development:** Contribute to the creation and maintenance of real-time dashboards that track key metrics and system performance. - **Data Engineering:** Support data cleaning, preprocessing, and organization tasks to make datasets ready for analysis. Write simple SQL queries and learn how to work with databases. - **Machine Learning:** Gain exposure to machine learning by assisting with model development and validation for autonomy applications - **Scientific Programming:** Learn to apply scientific and engineering programming techniques to develop small data pipelines, automate processes, and run simulations. - **Software Development:** Support software-related tasks such as building scripts or tools to improve workflows and automation. ### **What You'll Bring** - **Educational Background:** Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field. - **Technical Skills:** - Familiarity with Python for scientific programming (libraries such as NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Plotly, etc.). - Basic understanding of SQL for querying and working with data. - Exposure to software development practices (version control with Git, debugging, documentation) is a plus. - **Mathematical & Analytical Skills:** - Coursework or experience with statistics, linear algebra, or numerical methods. - Interest in applying engineering and data analysis to solve real-world problems. - **Problem-Solving:** - Curiosity and analytical thinking to approach technical challenges. - Ability to learn how to frame engineering problems as data science problems. - **Communication Skills:** - Willingness to communicate findings clearly with technical and non-technical teammates. - Strong written and verbal skills for documentation and presentations. - **Machine Learning & Data Modeling:** - description: Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles. Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet. # About the Role We are seeking talented engineers to work closely with the broader engineering team for an exciting internship opportunity. description: **The Role** We are excited to offer a unique opportunity for a diverse group of talented students to join the internship program at Schonfeld. Over the course of ten weeks, you will become an integral part of our Cybersecurity group within the Schonfeld Technology division. You will be immersed in Schonfeld’s collaborative culture, working alongside cybersecurity professionals on impactful, real-world projects addressing today’s most pressing threats. The Cybersecurity Department at Schonfeld is dedicated to safeguarding the firm’s data, assets, and reputation from both internal and external threats, while securely enabling the business to innovate and grow in an increasingly complex threat landscape. It includes Security Engineering, Security Operations, Governance, Risk, and Compliance teams. The Cybersecurity Operations team is seeking a hands-on individual who sets the standard for incident response, threat management and risk mitigation while driving continuous improvement of our security controls. **What You’ll Do** - **Incident Response** – Prepare for and assist in incident response. - **Threat Monitoring** – Continuous review of security alerts in partnership with vendors. - **Threat Hunting** – Identify previously undetected attacks. Feed detection pipeline and improve security posture. - **Threat Intelligence** – Analyze and incorporate actionable intel within detection, monitoring and hunting disciplines. Track and model adversaries to focus program activities. - **Vulnerability Management** – Monitor internal/external attack surface, validate vulnerabilities, and prioritize remediation. - **Security Posture** – Assess risk of changes to IT and security systems. Maintain coverage of controls and implement preventative/detective measures. Conduct risk assessments. - **Threat Detection** – Introduce new and enhance existing rules. Increase fidelity and create response runbooks. - **Automation** – Implement methods (SOAR and scripting) to speed delivery and maintain consistency. You’ll receive support from a dedicated manager and mentor, participate in team-building events, lunch-and-learns, social activities, and network with senior management. Summer-long projects will be directly related to the team’s work, culminating in a presentation to leadership. No prior finance experience required—just a passion for technology, curiosity about cybersecurity, and a drive to solve complex problems in a high-stakes environment. **What You’ll Bring** - A junior pursuing a degree in an Information Systems/Technology Risk /Cybersecurity field. - Someone who has demonstrated strong interest in the cybersecurity space through previous internships, part time jobs, extracurricular activities, and/or classes. - High levels of creativity and quick problem-solving capabilities - Strong interest in taking ownership of tasks/projects. - Strong analytical and organizational skills **Our Internship** Kick-start your career in finance with the Schonfeld Summer Internship! Over the course of 10 action-packed weeks, you will have the opportunity to build solutions that tackle real-world challenges and leave a lasting impact on the firm. As an intern, you’ll join a close-knit team that is ready to support your growth and accelerate your career. We will pair you with a dedicated manager and a mentor who’ll guide your development over the course of the internship and beyond. Throughout the program, you will have the chance to connect with senior leaders through a series of learning sessions, attend hands-on skills workshops, network at social events and get a behind-the-scenes look at how various functions power the firm. We’ll empower you to bring your ideas to life and make an impact. **Who We Are** Schonfeld is a global multi-manager hedge fund that strives to deliver industry-leading risk-adjusted returns for our investors. We leverage both internal and external portfolio manager teams around the world, seeking to capitalize on inefficiencies and opportunities within the markets. We draw from decades of experience and a significant investment in proprietary technology, infrastructure and risk analytics to invest across four main strategies: Quant, Tactical, Fundamental Equity and Discretionary Macro & Fixed Income. **Our Culture** At Schonfeld, we’ll invest in you. Attracting and retaining top talent is at the heart of what we do, because we believe that exceptional outcomes begin with exceptional people. We foster a culture where talent is empowered to continually learn, innovate and pursue ambitious goals. We are teamwork-oriented, collaborative and encourage ideas—at all levels—to be shared. As an organization committed to investing in our people, we provide learning and educational offerings and opportunities to make an impact. We encourage community through internal networks, external partnerships and service initiatives that promote inclusion and purpose beyond the firm’s walls. *The annual base pay for this role is expected to be between $85,000 and $95,000 which will be prorated based on internship start and end date. The expected base pay range is based on information at the time this post was generated. Actual compensation for the successful candidate will be determined based on a variety of factors such as skills, qualifications and experience and level of education.*

description: ![](https://click.appcast.io/greenhouse-te8/a31.png?ent=34&e=22630&t=1701374353806) ![](https://track.jobadx.com/v1/i.gif?utm_pixel=224e990b-8ff4-4287-8d5d-2ff09647f181&utm_ptz=EST&utm_rqt=track) ## About the Team DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt are one global team building the future of local commerce. Our products power millions of interactions between consumers, merchants, and couriers every day, in cities around the world. Together, we’re combining global scale with deep local understanding to deliver what’s next. At DoorDash, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across all three brands. We’re looking for students completing a bachelor’s or master’s degree to begin their engineering careers with DoorDash. You’ll help build and operate reliable, scalable technology that improves the experiences of consumers, merchants, and delivery partners across our global platform. Our Engineering team tackles complex technical challenges across a global, three-sided marketplace - from creating intuitive product experiences to designing the infrastructure and backend systems that help local commerce thrive. ## You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… You’ll work alongside a mentor, manager, and experienced engineers while contributing to real products and systems. As you build your technical knowledge, you’ll take on increasing ownership and see how your work affects the people and businesses using our platform. Here’s what your day-to-day might look like: - Develop, maintain, and ship production-ready software with support from your mentor and team - Write clean, testable code and contribute to code reviews, version control, and engineering best practices - Learn the systems and technical areas your work contributes to, including how they operate at scale - Apply feedback and coaching to strengthen your technical skills and problem-solving approach - Collaborate with engineers and cross-functional partners to solve problems for consumers, merchants, and delivery partners ## We’re excited about you because you have… - A bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science or a related discipline, graduating between Fall 2026 and Summer 2027 - At least two previous software engineering internships or equivalent practical experience, with no more than two years of full-time professional experience - Experience using at least one object-oriented programming language, such as Python, Java, or Kotlin - A solid understanding of algorithms and data structures - Experience working with databases and technologies such as SQL - Experience writing clean code, using version control, and creating unit tests ## **Nice to Have** - Curiosity about using AI-powered tools to support software development, problem-solving, and learning, alongside an understanding of how to evaluate their outputs and use them responsibly - Experience analyzing and improving the efficiency, scalability, or stability of software systems - Interest in developing, releasing, and operating large-scale web applications - Familiarity with systems monitoring, live deployments, or continuous integration - Experience solving real-time technology problems - Familiarity with service-oriented architecture, API development, or systems design ## **Why You’ll Love It Here** You’ll begin your career by contributing to technology used in the real world every day, with mentorship and support from experienced engineers. As your skills grow, so will the scope of the problems you can own. You’ll learn how large-scale systems behave in production, see the impact of what you build, and work with teammates across different disciplines, countries, and brands. ## **What We Offer** - Premium healthcare and comprehensive health benefits - Wellness expense reimbursement - Paid parental leave - Benefits and perks designed to support your health, wellbeing, and development **Compensation** The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others. To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page [here](https://careers.doordash.com/). See below for paid time off details: - **For salaried roles:** flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year. - **For hourly roles:** vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week). The national base pay range for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado. $107,400—$158,000 USD ## About DoorDash At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods. DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more. ## Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities.
